41	Five things were left to this ADR by the GDDs and by ADR-0008 and ADR-0009, and none can be decided inside a presenter story:
42	
43	1. **Scene shape.** Body's GDD (BDY-33) says a PROJECTOR owns one translation-only root per live body, with one y-sorted actor and props layer per root, and reparents Presenter nodes on `BODY_TRANSFER`. Layout's GDD (LY-31) says the default shape reparents section nodes under that root on every weld, that this "sits badly" with the Pipeline's single Y-sort scope, and that a spike should try a no-reparent option B first. Neither text knows whether nested Y-sort nodes form one scope, whether a weld should reparent or rebuild, or whether a tile map is per body or per section.
44	2. **The Y-sort key.** PR-5 fixes `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` and says the wall-face `y_sort_origin` "is set to the footprint depth, not 0". The engine's own key for a `TileMapLayer` cell is different (V3), the tie rule is tree order (V1), nothing registers the `entity_id` namespaces that make ids unique across blocks (Layout OQ-33), and a door's sort edge depends on a Graph value (TR-pxl-007).
45	3. **Weld, cut and arrival cost.** A weld must show its bead in the first frame (TR-assembly-045), cost at most 8 ms P99 (TR-shipbody-045, a working threshold) and leave no orphan node; an arrival must build the largest destination scene inside the settle window (TR-webmap-037); both are budgeted in `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` units that no ADR has made precise. ADR-0009 OQ-I left the weld case to this ADR.
46	4. **The camera-limits rectangle.** ADR-0009 OQ-C reconciled that a PROJECTOR publishes the rectangle and never writes `Camera2D.limit_*`; no ADR has named the sink, the frame, or the rectangle.
47	5. **Draw bands and the fallback.** The z-band order is "the contract" and the numbers are "the ADR's" (PR-5); the per-row fallback is built only if it wins a measurement (TR-pxl-009).
48	
49	### Constraints
50	- **Presentation never writes the simulation (kernel H4).** The PROJECTOR writes only engine-side derived objects its block owners' GDDs name, never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D` (the Layout projector; ADR-0009 § 1), and never writes `Camera2D.limit_*` (OQ-C).
51	- **Integer placement, one assignment point.** Every `Node2D.position` in presentation is written only through `Placement.put` (ADR-0009 § 4); canvas coordinates are integer-valued `float32` and exact for `|v| <= 2^24` base px (ADR-0008 § 6.2); body-frame and canvas offsets are bounded by ADR-0015 (`WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`).
52	- **Rotation is never rendered inside (C2).** Every body root has rotation 0, scale (1, 1), skew 0.
53	- **`physics_interpolation` is off for all presentation (ADR-0009 § 5); `tick_alpha` is the one interpolator.**
54	- **Stage `PROJECT` (0) runs before `CAMERA_SOLVE` (1) in the same `_process` pass** (ADR-0009 § 3), so anything the projector publishes is consumed in the same frame. The registration order inside stage 0 is the layout projector, then `body.projector`, then Lighting's occluder builder (ADR-0009 § 3).
55	- **Presenters define no `_process` and no handler allocates or draws** (ADR-0009 § 2): the projectors mark dirty in the handler and build in `present`.
56	- **The PROJECTOR scripts live in `src/presentation/projector/`; `src/sim/**` is tree-free** (ADR-0010 § 1.2). Pure packing helpers that the simulation must also compute live in `src/shared/` (L0).
57	- **Section offsets are on the 24 px grid, not the 48 px grid** (ADR-0013 § 7, `GRID_24`; the registry's MVP socket pair gives an offset of 696 px on x, which is 14.5 tiles).
58	- **Walls project up-screen** (PR-5 convention): footprint rows `[y0, y0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`, a face of `WALL_FACE_PX` rising from the footprint's south edge, a cap of `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` above the face.
59	- **Release-export performance is unmeasured (OQ-10); every wall-clock figure here is a proposal or margin evidence.**
60	
61	### Requirements
62	- One tree shape that the weld, cut, pod hop, arrival, restore and salvage paths all produce identically (a test compares an incrementally updated projector with a fresh one fed `ALL`).
63	- A draw order that is a pure function of persisted ids and positions: identical on 10 runs and after a save and reload that reverses creation order (PR-5 acceptance).
64	- A weld frame that moves nodes and shifts positions without building tiles; an arrival that builds in a declared number of frames.
65	- Named bands and a lint that dependents can use without writing a z number.
66	- A limits rectangle in integer base px, in the frame the solver works in, published before the solve.
67	
68	### Binding stances respected (registry check, `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`)
69	No registered stance is contradicted. Stances this ADR builds on: `PresentationStage` constants and the PROJECT order (ADR-0009); `Placement.at` / `put` as the only position writer (ADR-0009 § 4); `camera_canvas_transform_write` (ADR-0008: the solver is the only clamp, `Camera2D.limit_*` untouched, no `Camera2D` in the world tree); canvas exactness to `2^24` (ADR-0008 § 6.2); the layer-first source tree with `src/presentation/projector/` (ADR-0010); ids are block-local and the kernel allocates none (ADR-0003 § 2). One registry-adjacent point is **extended**, not contradicted: the registered constant `LAYOUT_ID_NS` is "to be agreed" in `entities.yaml`; § 4 fixes it. ADR-0003's "entity ids are block-local" rule stands: the `entity_id` of this ADR is a **presentation sort-key composite**, never a block id and never persisted.
70	
71	## Decision
72	
73	### Architecture Diagram
74	
75	```
76	 stage 0 PROJECT (ADR-0009 § 3), one rendered frame, in this registration order
77	 |
78	 |-(1) Layout projector (PROJECTOR facet; subscribes layout.state only; reads door_passage and the rect table)
79	 |       dirty keys SEC / BODY / SEAM / LEAF / ALL  ->  per-section SectionScene objects (RefCounted handles)
80	 |       builds in the hidden Staging holder, <= BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME work units a frame, commits atomically
81	 |       never parents under a body root: it hands finished SectionScenes to body.projector
82	 |
83	 |-(2) body.projector (PROJECTOR facet; subscribes body.state, layout.state, web.state)
84	 |       BodyRoot per body in the ProjectionSet; mounts / moves SectionScenes; reparents + shifts on weld and cut;
85	 |       attach / attach_presenter / detach; writes root canvas offsets; WM-19 visibility;
86	 |       publishes CameraLimits (integer rect) and ProjectorReadiness
87	 |
88	 |-(3) Lighting occluder builder (ADR-0028)  -- unchanged by this ADR; reads the rect table, not these nodes
89	 v
90	 stage 1 CAMERA_SOLVE reads CameraLimits in the same frame
91	 stage 2.. AVATAR / TRAIL / ... write positions of nodes they attached (Placement.put)
92	
93	 scene tree under the WorldViewport (ADR-0008 § 2)       y = y_sort_enabled, z = z_index (absolute here: parents are z 0)
94	 ProjectorRoot : Node2D                                  not sorted, z 0
95	 +- Staging : Node2D                                     visible = false, IN the tree (no orphan noise), never drawn
96	 +- World : Node2D                                       y = TRUE   (the one sort scope's top)
97	    +- BodyRoot[body_id ascending] : Node2D              y = TRUE, translation only, rotation 0, scale (1,1), skew 0
98	         position = canvas_offset_render(body); visible = InteriorDrawRule (WM-19)
99	         |- Floor        : Node2D  z = ZBand.FLOOR  (0)    y = false   per-section floor TileMapLayer (position = section_offset)
100	         |- Marks        : Node2D  z = ZBand.MARKS  (1)    y = false   foreign: floor trails, stains (Failure & Trail)
101	         |- Faces        : Node2D  z = ZBand.YSORT (10)    y = TRUE    class_rank 0: per-section wall-face TileMapLayer
102	         |- Mounted      : Node2D  z = ZBand.YSORT (10)    y = TRUE    class_rank 1: per-section mounted TileMapLayer, then sorted sprites
103	         |- PropsActors  : Node2D  z = ZBand.YSORT (10)    y = TRUE    class_rank 2 then 3, children in (class_rank, entity_id) order
104	         |- Caps         : Node2D  z = ZBand.CAPS  (20)    y = false   per-section cap TileMapLayer
105	         '- Dust         : Node2D  z = ZBand.DUST  (30)    y = false   foreign: dust, mist, venting (never Y-sorted)
106	
107	 merged sort scope = every node on a chain of y_sort_enabled ancestors from World down to a sorted group (V2);
108	 cross-body equal keys fall to BodyRoot order (body_id ascending); within a body the group order Faces < Mounted < PropsActors
109	 is the class-rank order, and inside PropsActors child order is (class_rank, entity_id).
110	```
111	
112	### 1. The decisions at a glance
113	
114	| Point (from the scope) | Decision | Where |
115	|---|---|---|
116	| Per-body roots | **Yes.** One `y_sort_enabled`, translation-only `BodyRoot` per body in the `ProjectionSet`, under one `y_sort_enabled` `World`. The root, not each node, carries the canvas offset. | § 2 |
117	| Reparent versus rebuild | **Reparent and shift** every moved section's nodes on weld and cut; **no tile is rebuilt**. Rebuild (chunked, staged, atomic) happens only on first build, arrival, restore, `ALL`, and a section whose template or discard state changed. A fresh-build path stays the reference: a signature test requires both paths to give equal scenes. | § 7 |
118	| Per-body versus per-section `TileMapLayer` | **Per section**, one layer per layer kind (floor, wall face, mounted, cap), **exactly one `TileSetAtlasSource` each**. | § 5 |
119	| Y-sort key | `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` realised as: engine key = integer node position (sprites) or `cell_top + tile_h/2 + origins` (tiles); class rank = group order; `entity_id` = child order of the sorted layers. Door and wall sort edges as in § 3. | § 3 |
120	| `entity_id` namespaces | `EntityId.pack(ns, local)` in `src/shared/`; namespace bytes **LAYOUT 1, BODY 2, INTERACTION 3, HORROR 4, SUIT 5, WEB 6, TRAIL 7**, 8 to 127 reserved append-only; Layout's local part as LY-31. | § 4 |
121	| Camera-limit rectangle | Integer base-px rect of the avatar's body: union of `[offset, offset + size_tiles x TILE_PX)` over its sections, grown north by `WALL_FACE_PX + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`, published as `CameraLimits` in stage `PROJECT`; the solver is the only clamp. | § 9 |
122	| SP-YSORT-1 | Confirms; does not choose. | § 11 |
123	
124	### 2. The scene tree
125	
126	The tree in the diagram is the contract. Rules, each lint- or boot-checked (§ Validation):
127	
128	- **`World` and every `BodyRoot` have `y_sort_enabled = true`.** That is what makes the sort scope one merged group across bodies (V2). A `BodyRoot` is never made non-sorting: a non-sorting intermediate sorts its whole subtree as a unit (V2, P4), which would turn cross-body ordering into root order.
129	- **`BodyRoot` is translation only**: `rotation == 0`, `scale == (1, 1)`, `skew == 0` every frame (TR-pxl-018, C2 consequence (i)); only `Placement.put` writes `position`. A detached section keeps rotation 0 and simply gets its own root (TR-pxl-018 "detached sections translate without rotation").
130	- **Seven groups per root, in the order drawn above, created with the root and freed with it.** `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors` are the only sorting groups. `Floor`, `Marks`, `Caps` and `Dust` have `y_sort_enabled = false`; their z band keeps them out of the sort (V4). The PR-5 lint "the cap `TileMapLayer` is not a child of the Y-sort node" is therefore restated by band, not by ancestry (GDD sync).
131	- **`z_index` is set once, on the group, from `ZBand` names; `z_as_relative` stays at its default `true` and every ancestor of a group has z 0**, so the group's z is its absolute z. No other node writes `z_index`, and no presenter writes a z number (lint `PJT-03`).
132	- **The `World` node is the only Y-sort scope for the interior.** Exterior and transit layers (parallax, silhouettes, the pod in transit) are the camera host's and the Web Map presenter's and are not under `World`; the projector creates no exterior layer (TR-pxl-018, owned by ADR-0008).
133	
134	**The z bands (names are the contract, TR-pxl-008).**
135	
136	| Name | z | Sorted | Group | Contents |
137	|---|---|---|---|---|
138	| `ZBand.FLOOR` | 0 | never | `Floor` | floor `TileMapLayer`s; grates and drains |
139	| `ZBand.MARKS` | +1 | never | `Marks` | floor trails, stains, footprints (foreign, Trail); drawn flat, authoring order |
140	| `ZBand.YSORT` | +10 | yes | `Faces`, `Mounted`, `PropsActors` | wall faces; wall-mounted items and wall trails; doors, props, machinery, actors, horrors, deployables, empty suits, off-floor web pieces |
141	| `ZBand.CAPS` | +20 | never | `Caps` | cap `TileMapLayer`s; free-hanging housings |
142	| `ZBand.DUST` | +30 | never | `Dust` | `GPUParticles2D` (foreign) |
143	
144	Floor marks and wall trails keep the PR-5 assignment: floor trails at `MARKS` and never sorted; wall trails in `Mounted` at their host face's sort origin (TR-ftrail-017); "no trail uses z 0 or +20" holds because a trail node can only be attached to `MARKS`, `Mounted` or `Dust` and the projector, not the trail, sets z. All five values sit inside the default `Light2D` range of -1024 to 1024, which is inclusive and was probed (V6); Lighting (ADR-0028) must set every light's `range_z_min <= ZBand.FLOOR` and `range_z_max >= ZBand.DUST`, and the fallback table of § 10 raises the largest value to 910, still inside. The numeric values live in one file, `src/presentation/projector/z_band.gd`, and dependents lint names, never numbers.
145	
146	**Caps-above safety (TR-pxl-008).** Caps draw above the sorted band, which is correct iff no item flush against a wall has a face taller than `WALL_FACE_PX`. This is a kit rule; the debug tree-walk keeps the GDD's `diag.cap_overlap` (a prop whose drawn height exceeds the face) and `diag.actor_in_footprint` (a foot row inside a wall footprint) as dev and test checks in `ProjectorAudit`.
147	
148	### 3. The Y-sort key, as built
149	
150	The contract key is `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` with class ranks 0 wall-face tiles, 1 wall-mounted items, 2 doors, props, machinery, deployables, empty suits and off-floor web pieces, 3 actors and horrors. Godot gives us the first term and the tree order; the other two are realised by structure:

150	The contract key is `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` with class ranks 0 wall-face tiles, 1 wall-mounted items, 2 doors, props, machinery, deployables, empty suits and off-floor web pieces, 3 actors and horrors. Godot gives us the first term and the tree order; the other two are realised by structure:
151	
152	| Term | Realised by |
153	|---|---|
154	| `sort_y` | The engine key: a node's accumulated y for a `Node2D`; for a `TileMapLayer` cell, `cell_top + tile_size.y / 2 + TileData.y_sort_origin + TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin + layer.position.y` (V3). All terms are integers. |
155	| `class_rank` | The order of the sorted groups under a body root (`Faces` before `Mounted` before `PropsActors`) plus, inside `PropsActors`, rank 2 children before rank 3 children. An equal key ties by tree order (V1), so the earlier group draws first. |
156	| `entity_id` | The child order of a sorted layer. Children are kept in ascending `(class_rank, entity_id)` by `SortedLayer` (§ 3.3), so an equal key and rank resolve by `entity_id` ascending, never by `x` and never by creation order. |
157	
158	**3.1 Sort origins (integer base px, TR-pxl-006).**
159	- **Actors and horrors**: the foot row. The Presenter writes the node `position` to the integer `(p.x, p.y)` (BDY-33 (e)), so the key is `y_foot`, already floored by `Placement.at`; an actor at 239.6 sorts as 239.
160	- **Walls, doors, props, machinery nodes**: the south edge of the footprint.
161	- **Anything mounted on a wall face** (pipes, fittings, seams, gauges, the emissive overlay, wall trails, bead, plate, scar): its host face's sort origin, drawn after the face by group order.
162	- **Doors and doorways (TR-pxl-007).** `sort_y = y_0` (the footprint's north edge) when the doorway is open, and `sort_y = y_0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` when it is closed (a closed door sorts as a wall). The projector computes it in `DoorSort.sort_y(y0, open_extent_px)` (a pure function) from Layout's `door_passage_into(section_id, via_id, out)` record (`open_extent_px`, ADR-0013 § 8 and § 11), and writes the leaf sprite's position through `Placement.put` when it re-reads the leaf on a `LEAF/<section_id>` key (ADR-0013 § 8 marks LEAF whenever a leaf rect changes, and `area` leaving zero changes the leaf rect). Reading the Layout record, not the Graph, means the Layout projector subscribes to `layout.state` alone (the Graph dirties keys every step and would wake stage 0 needlessly) and needs no edge-id reverse lookup; for a mated hatch the record is read once per section, so both leaves agree. **Equivalence with `area > 0`:** D.5 defines `open_extent_px = gap(area)`, which is 0 when closed and positive for every `area >= 1` provided the authored `area_max` does not exceed the doorway width in px; a larger `area_max` would draw a barely-open leaf at its closed edge, so an `area_max <= doorway width` invariant is asked of ADR-0013 (OQ-E). The leaf sprite's drawn extent equals the leaf rect with no tween (TR-section-013).
163	
164	**3.2 The tile convention (a GDD-sync item, PR-5).** The engine measures `y_sort_origin` from the **cell centre**, not the cell top (V3). The GDD text "set to the footprint depth, not 0" is therefore right only for one cell convention. This ADR pins it: **wall-face and wall-mounted `TileMapLayer`s use a cell height of `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`** (one 24-row GRID_24 row; the cell width is the art bible's cell rule and does not enter the key), `TileData.y_sort_origin = 0` on every tile, and the **layer's** `y_sort_origin = WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH / 2` (one value per layer; boot invariant `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` is even). A wall whose footprint is rows `[y0, y0 + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)` sits in cell row `y0 / WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (GRID_24), so its key is `y0 + depth / 2 + depth / 2 = y0 + depth`, the south edge, and the PR-5 acceptance example (footprint rows 240 to 264, key 264) holds. The 72 px face and 24 px cap art is taller than the cell and hangs up-screen through the tile's `texture_origin`, which does not enter the key (V3). The floor and cap layers are never sorted, so they need no origin.
165	
166	**3.3 `SortedLayer`: how `(class_rank, entity_id)` order is kept.**
167	
168	```gdscript
169	# src/presentation/projector/sorted_layer.gd
170	class_name SortedLayer extends RefCounted
171	## Wraps one sorted group node. Children are kept in ascending (class_rank, entity_id); the parallel arrays hold the order.
172	var _nodes: Array[Node2D]
173	var _rank: PackedByteArray
174	var _eid: PackedInt64Array
175	func insert(node: Node2D, class_rank: int, entity_id: int) -> int   ## OK or ERR_DUPLICATE_ID; binary search, add_child, move_child to the index
176	func remove(node: Node2D) -> bool                                     ## removes from the parallel arrays; does not free
177	func merge_from(other: SortedLayer) -> void                           ## one pass: both inputs are sorted, so compute final indices, then move_child once per node
178	func count() -> int
179	```
180	`insert` finds the index by binary search over `(rank, eid)`, calls `add_child` and then `move_child(node, index)`; a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)` is refused (counted as `diag.sort_id_collision`, which must stay zero) rather than silently ordered by tree position. `merge_from` serves the weld: the survivor's and the absorbed body's `PropsActors` are each already sorted, so the merged order is one linear pass followed by one `move_child` per node (V9: 100 moves cost 0.05 ms on the dev machine). **Tiles carry no `entity_id`**: wall-face and wall-mounted tiles are rank 0 and 1 and tie among themselves by cell position, which is the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`; the sprites of rank 1 are children of `Mounted` after its tile layers.
181	
182	**3.4 Cross-body equal keys (a stated exception).** Within a body the order is exactly the contract. Across two bodies whose interiors are both drawn (docked, WM-19) an equal key with overlapping sprites falls to `BodyRoot` order, ascending `body_id`, which the projector maintains with `move_child`. For Layout pieces that coincides with ascending `entity_id` whenever section ids and body ids were allocated in the same order, which holds for the MVP builds (`init_world` builds home first); it is not guaranteed after cuts. The region where this can occur is the mating seam of two docked hulls. It is tested as a bounded exception (AC-123 (b) is run within one body; the cross-body case is a recorded SP-YSORT-1 observation, § 11) and listed in Risks.
183	
184	### 4. `entity_id` and its namespaces
185	
186	`entity_id` is **a presentation sort-key composite**, not a block id. It is a pure function of persisted ids, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one and is never stored. ADR-0003's rule (ids are block-local, cross-block references are `(block_id, entity_id)`) is unchanged.
187	
188	```gdscript
189	# src/shared/entity_id.gd (L0: pure ints, no engine types; sim modules and presentation both may call it)
190	class_name EntityId extends RefCounted
191	const NS_SHIFT: int = 56
192	const LOCAL_MASK: int = (1 << 56) - 1
193	static func pack(ns: int, local: int) -> int           ## (ns << 56) | local; ns in 1..127; local in 0..LOCAL_MASK; asserts in debug, returns 0 (invalid) otherwise
194	static func ns_of(id: int) -> int
195	static func local_of(id: int) -> int
196	static func layout_local(section_id: int, kind_ordinal: int, idx: int) -> int   ## (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | idx
197	# src/shared/entity_ns.gd : the namespace table (append-only; a golden test pins it)
198	class_name EntityNs extends RefCounted
199	const LAYOUT: int = 1       # door leaf, jamb, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar sprites
200	const BODY: int = 2         # actors (local = actor_id)
201	const INTERACTION: int = 3  # loose items, deployables (local = item_id)
202	const HORROR: int = 4       # horror rigs (local = horror entity_id)
203	const SUIT: int = 5         # empty suits and carried-and-dropped suit props
204	const WEB: int = 6          # off-floor web pieces
205	const TRAIL: int = 7        # trail sprites (local = the Graph subject key)
206	# 8..127: reserved, append-only
207	```
208	- **The sign.** A namespace byte of 1 to 127 keeps every id positive in GDScript's signed 64-bit `int`, so ids compare as plain integers (the Pipeline never needs an unsigned compare). `0` is invalid.
209	- **Layout's local part** is LY-31's: `section_id` below `2^20` (ADR-0013 § 3 guarantees it), `kind_ordinal` in 8 bits, `idx` in 16 bits (the rect `idx` or the template placement index, below the rect stride, ADR-0013 § 13). `kind_ordinal` values are assigned append-only: `DOOR_LEAF 1`, `PROP 2`, `MACHINE 3`, `BEAD 4`, `PLATE 5`, `SCAR 6`, and **`JAMB 7`**, which TR-assembly-045 requires and ADR-0013 § 13's closed list of six does not name (an assumption on ADR-0013, in `cross_adr_assumptions`). Class ranks: `BEAD`, `PLATE`, `SCAR` are rank 1 (the wall-mounted layer, LY-33); `DOOR_LEAF`, `JAMB`, `PROP`, `MACHINE` are rank 2.
210	- **Other publishers' local parts** are their own persisted ids: Body's `actor_id` (an `int64` counter, asserted below `2^56`), Interaction's `item_id`, Horror's `entity_id`. Each publisher calls `EntityId.pack` itself; Layout exports no helper (ADR-0013 § 13), so the Layout projector packs, using only persisted ids.
211	- **Ordering consequence.** At an equal key and rank, namespaces order ascending: a Layout prop draws before an Interaction item, a Body actor before a horror. That is deterministic and save-stable; it is a convention, not a design claim.
212	- **Guard.** `SortedLayer.insert` refuses a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)`; a golden test pins the namespace table; a lint forbids `EntityId.pack` with a literal namespace outside `entity_ns.gd` (`PJT-08`).
213	
214	### 5. Section scenes: per-section layers, one atlas each
215	
216	**Per-section `TileMapLayer`, decided by arithmetic.** Section offsets lie on the 24 px grid and welded sections are placed by `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b` (ADR-0013 § 7). The registry's MVP pair gives a 696 px offset, which is 14.5 floor tiles, so the cells of two welded sections do not share one 48 px cell grid and **no single per-body tile map can hold both**. Each section therefore owns its own layers, positioned at its integer `section_offset`. Other reasons point the same way and are secondary: a `SEC` change, a discard (LM4) or a dormancy change rebuilds or frees one section only; the maintained and `_worn` atlases (DA-5) differ per section, so a merged layer would mix two atlas sources, and V8 shows that is the expensive case.
217	
218	**The layers per section** (up to four `TileMapLayer`s, each `tile_set` shared across sections of the same atlas set and layer kind through a `TileSetCache` keyed `(atlas_set, layer_kind)`):

221	|---|---|---|---|---|
222	| floor | `Floor` | no | `TILE_PX` square, `rendering_quadrant_size` 16 (ADR-0008 § 7.1) | n/a |

225	| cap | `Caps` | no | 48 x 24 slices (PR-5 z-band table) | n/a |

227	**One atlas source per layer (mandatory).** Each `TileSet` used by a layer holds exactly one `TileSetAtlasSource`. V8 is the reason: the same 453 cells read 1 draw call from one source and 440 from two sources that alternate by row. Sprites use `AtlasTexture` regions of the same sheet so they batch with it; a `_worn` section uses the `_worn` sheet, so a draw-call boundary appears at the section boundary only. This is a production rule for the asset spec (art bible 8.4 to 8.6) and a boot check in the `TileSetCache`.

229	**Atlas selection by template (TR-derelict-028, DA-5).** A presentation table `assets/data/presentation/atlas_map.json` (a new data domain for ADR-0007; integer-only, closed schema, manifest-listed) maps `template_id` to `atlas_set` in `{MAINTAINED, WORN}`. 233	**Two projectors, one handoff.** The Layout projector builds and owns a `SectionScene` per live section; `body.projector` owns bodies and roots and mounts scenes. A `SectionScene` exposes `mount(body_root_set, section_offset)` and `unmount()` that only `body.projector` calls; when the Layout projector later swaps a rebuilt layer it asks the scene to `swap_in`, and the scene replaces its node under whatever parent it is currently mounted on. 252	### 6. Building: work units, staging, atomic commit, readiness
253	
254	**Work unit.** One `TileMapLayer.set_cell` call or one sprite node created and configured is one **work unit**. The knob `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` (a Layout GDD tuning knob, read from the frozen `LayoutTuning` table, ADR-0007 § 1.5; the module source carries no literal) is the units per `present` call. The unit is named after tiles because tiles dominate (the GDD's tile counts for the MVP world and for the largest destination scene are its sizing basis); sprites are counted in it so that "builds N tiles in at most M frames" (TR-section-024) remains true with sprites included. The number of frames for a build of `U` units is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)`, plus one if the final commit needs its own `present`.
255	
256	**Order, inside one section.** Floor cells, wall-face cells, mounted cells, cap cells, then sprites in ascending `(kind_ordinal, idx)`. Sections build in ascending `section_id`. A chunk may end at any unit.
257	
258	**Staging and atomic commit.** A new or rebuilt section builds under the `Staging` holder (in the tree, `visible = false`, so `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` stays flat, V7) and `complete` flips only on the last unit. `body.projector` mounts a scene only when `complete`, in one pass, so no frame draws half a section. A rebuild of an already mounted section (a salvage that changes its template-visible state) builds a second set in `Staging`, keeps drawing the old set until the last chunk, then swaps (`swap_in`) in one apply; the same "old complete state keeps drawing" rule ADR-0009 § 2 states for the PROJECTOR. This ADR adds no exemption to the chunk budget for the Layout projector or `body.projector`: the single-chunk in-reach exemption in ADR-0009 § 1 belongs to Lighting's occluder builder only.
259	
260	**What is not chunked.** Anything a weld or cut needs in the first frame: reparenting and shifting nodes (§ 7), the socket-state sprites (bead, jambs, leaf, plate, scar: a handful of sprites, not tiles), root creation and freeing, the limits publish. These run in the stage-0 call that follows the notification, so the bead is drawn in the first rendered frame whose committed tick is at least the apply tick (TR-assembly-045); no bead sprite exists while `welds[]` has no row because the sprite set is built from `welds[]` and nothing else. The "last-projected cache" of the door leaf (ADR-0013 § 8) is read, not written, by the projector.
261	
262	**Readiness.**
263	
264	```gdscript

266	class_name ProjectorReadiness extends RefCounted
267	var scene_epoch: int          # +1 on every complete commit or mount change
268	var pending_units: int        # work units still queued, all bodies in the ProjectionSet
269	var late_count: int           # ARRIVE_SCENE_LATE occurrences (DIAGNOSTIC only, never a SIM notification)
270	func is_ready() -> bool       # pending_units == 0 and every ProjectionSet section is complete and mounted
271	```
272	`PipelineRoot` reads `is_ready()` for the TRANSIT_HOLD latch (WM-14: "the Pipeline may cut to the avatar once its own projector latch also holds"; ADR-0008 is asked to add the read). When `DERELICT_LOADED` (or the arrival's `pod_settle`) is delivered while `is_ready()` is false, the projector increments `late_count`, logs `ARRIVE_SCENE_LATE`, and keeps building; the simulation is never delayed (E-19, TR-webmap-037). The arrival's worst-case build is the largest destination scene, home plus the welded derelict; its frame count is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)` with `U` counted from the real sections (a test builds it through `build_section`, not a hand sum), and `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` must cover it by the Web Map lint formula, whose numerator becomes the projector's work-unit count (tiles plus sprites) of the largest destination scene, not tiles alone (GDD Sync).
273	
274	**The projection set.** Scenes exist exactly for the sections the `ProjectionSet` names: the avatar's body (so the pod interior exists during a leg), the loaded set, and the arrival target while `ARRIVING` (it is still dormant then, WM-14). `body.projector` reads the avatar's body as `body_of_actor(actor_of_seat(local_seat))` from `BodyView` (the seat is injected at `setup()`), and the rest from a Web Map read (an assumption on ADR-0026: `web.view` publishes `projection_sections_into(out: PackedInt32Array) -> int`, ascending, including the arriving target). A section leaving the set is **freed** at the end of the next stage-0 pass, not hidden (a departed destination is rebuilt on return, which is the case the GDD sizes `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` for); retaining hidden scenes is a possible later knob, not built.

276	### 7. Weld, cut, pod hop, restore: reparent and shift, rebuild as the reference
277	
278	**Decision.** On a weld or cut the projector **moves** the affected sections' existing nodes to their new body root and shifts their positions by the Layout-reported `frame_shift_px`; it **rebuilds no tile**. Rebuilding the whole destination scene on every weld was rejected (Alternative 4): it spends a chunked build, shows a frame boundary, makes two code paths for the same tree anyway, and gives no benefit because a moved section's geometry does not change.
279

279	
280	**The primitive.**
281	
282	```gdscript
283	# src/presentation/projector/scene_move.gd
284	class_name SceneMove extends RefCounted
285	## The one way to change a presentation node's parent. Local position is kept (reparent(p, false), probed; remove_child + add_child is equivalent). Never the one-argument reparent.
286	static func to(node: Node, new_parent: Node) -> void:
287		node.reparent(new_parent, false)
288	```
289	`Node.reparent(p)` with its default `keep_global_transform = true` rewrites the local position (V5), which would put a moved sprite at the wrong place, so it is banned outside this helper (`PJT-04`); TR-shipbody-032's "without using global-transform-preserving `Node.reparent`" is satisfied literally. After a move the node is the last child of its new parent; `SortedLayer` re-establishes order.
290	
291	**Weld (`AttachResult`, ADR-0013 § 7; `BODY_TRANSFER{weld}` and `BODY_DOCK_CONTACT`, ADR-0015).** In the stage-0 call that follows the notification, `body.projector`:
292	1. Reads the new `bodies[]` and `section_offset` of each section (Layout views). For every `SectionScene` whose `mounted_body_id` differs from `body_of(section_id)`, computes `delta = new_offset - mounted_off`, which equals the `frame_shift_px` of the weld for every moved section.
293	2. Moves the scene's four layer nodes to the matching group of the survivor root with `SceneMove.to`, and writes each layer's `position = new_offset` with `Placement.put`.
294	3. Moves the scene's `layout_sprites` to the survivor's `Mounted` or `PropsActors` `SortedLayer` according to class rank, shifting each by `delta` with `Placement.put(node, Vector2i(node.position) + delta)`, using `merge_from` so order is one pass.
295	4. Moves every **foreign attachment** whose `section_id` is a moved section the same way (§ 7.1), and every attached Presenter whose actor has a `BODY_TRANSFER` record to the destination `PropsActors` layer (the Presenter writes its own position later in stage 2, from `pos_curr` in the destination frame).
296	5. The socket-state sprites the weld changed (bead, jambs, leaf, plate, scar) were **already built by the Layout projector earlier in the same stage-0 pass** (it runs first, § 5), unchunked, from `welds[]` and the socket rows, into the still-mounted `SectionScene`s whose `static_version` moved; `body.projector` moves them with their scenes in steps 2 and 3 and builds nothing itself.
297	6. Frees the dissolved body's root (its groups are empty by now; a non-empty group is a defect, counted `PJT_ROOT_NOT_EMPTY`), recomputes and publishes `CameraLimits` (§ 9), updates every root's canvas offset (the canvas origin is now the survivor's frame), and bumps `scene_epoch`.
298	
299	The weld frame's cost is therefore proportional to nodes moved, not tiles built (V9 margin: the two reparent probes cost 0.08 to 0.3 ms on the dev machine). The node count after a weld equals the count before minus one root (`OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` flat, AC-BDY-92). The sort order of any sprite relative to a wall is unchanged because every key shifts by the same constant (the canvas origin change) and within-body relations are preserved; exact equal-key ties across the two bodies are the § 3.4 exception.
300	
301	**Cut (`DetachResult`, ADR-0013 § 7).** The mirror: a new `BodyRoot` for the new `body_id`, the moved components' scenes and foreign attachments moved and shifted by the re-base (`delta = offset_new - offset_old`), `BODY_TRANSFER{detach}` actors moved, limits recomputed for the avatar's body, and the new body's interior is hidden unless the avatar is on it (WM-19).
302	
303	**Pod hop.** Nothing is built or moved (a pod hop builds nothing, Web Map CF-LY); `BODY_TRANSFER{pod}` moves only the actor's Presenter node, and the camera cuts (ADR-0008 § 6.1). The canvas origin changes to the new avatar body, so every root's canvas offset is rewritten.
304	
305	**Restore, new game, `ALL`.** `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` frees every scene and root and rebuilds from the views through the same build path (staged, chunked, atomic). `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so nothing interpolates across the break. A scripted weld, cut and pod sequence through an incrementally updated projector and a fresh projector fed `ALL` must give equal `rebuild_signature()` values (ADR-0009 § 2 safety net, mandatory here: the projector is the first key-level incremental presenter whose two paths differ in kind).

326	### 8. Body roots: canvas offset and visibility
327	
328	**Canvas offset (the formula ADR-0015 hands to this ADR).** For every body root, with `avatar_body` the avatar's current body, `off_curr(b) = world(b) - world(avatar_body)` and `off_prev(b) = world_prev(b) - world_prev(avatar_body)` using the **current** avatar body for both terms (so a body switch never interpolates across two reference frames), and `position = Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, frame.alpha)`, written with `Placement.put` in stage 0 (`world`, `world_prev`, `vel` come from `BodyView`; `world` is exterior-only and bounded by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`, so every offset is within `2^23` and exact in `float32`). The avatar's body root is at (0, 0). A root whose offset did not change costs one skipped write.
329	
330	**Visibility (WM-19, defence in depth).** `BodyRoot.visible = InteriorDrawRule.visible(b, avatar_body, ...)`: true for the avatar's body and for a body docked or welded to it; false for a body drawn only as an exterior silhouette (those are not this tree). The rule is a pure function with injected inputs so it is unit-testable; its docked input is a Web Map read (an assumption on ADR-0026). Hiding a root hides its subtree and its lights' occluders are Lighting's concern.
331	
332	### 9. The camera-limit rectangle
333	
334	- **Value.** `CameraLimits` is a `RefCounted` with `valid`, `min_x`, `min_y`, `max_x`, `max_y` (integers, base px, half-open on the max side), `body_id` and `epoch`. `body.projector` is its only writer; `CameraSolver` (stage 1) reads it from `SolverInput` and is the only clamp. `Camera2D.limit_*` is never written (OQ-C closed, TR-pxl-017).
335	- **Frame.** The canvas is the avatar's body frame with the avatar's body at the origin (C2), so the rectangle is expressed in the avatar's body frame, which is also the canvas frame.
336	- **Rectangle.** The union, over `sections_of(avatar_body)`, of `[section_offset, section_offset + size_tiles x TILE_PX)` per axis (the template's `size_tiles`), grown on the **north** edge by `LIMITS_NORTH_OVERHANG = WALL_FACE_PX + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (a derived constant from two registered names; it lets the camera reach the top of the north wall's face and cap, which project up-screen above the footprint, PR-5). The three other edges are the hull envelope: "the void beyond a hull is honest black". No authored rect means `valid = false` and no clamp. The rectangle is **integer base px**; the solver's easing (`rect_eff`) and the inner-box-first order are ADR-0008's.
337	- **When.** Published in stage `PROJECT` on weld, cut, load, `ALL`, any `BODY`/`SEC` key of the avatar's body, and on a `BODY_TRANSFER` that changes the avatar's body; `epoch` increments on every change so the solver eases a changed rectangle and never pops it, except on a camera cut. Because stage 0 runs before stage 1, the solver consumes the new rectangle in the same frame as the `BODY_TRANSFER` rebase, in the new body's frame.
338	- **Clamp consequences owned elsewhere.** `CLAMPED` state, `world_to_hud` never offset while clamped, and the JOLT rule (at most `JOLT_PX`'s range, default 0, P1 events only, inside the viewport, never a container offset) are ADR-0008's; this ADR only guarantees that the projector never moves the camera and never offsets the canvas for a limit.

340	### 10. The per-row z-band fallback (TR-pxl-009): specified, not built
341	
342	At MVP the sorted band is the single scope of § 2 and **the fallback is not built**. The reason is a probe-backed expectation, not a measurement: draw calls follow texture runs along the sorted order (V8), and with one sheet per layer the sorted layer is a handful of runs per row in view; the GDD's own 50 to 300 estimate is "NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike". The decision rule is the GDD's, made explicit:
343	
344	- **Trigger.** `D_ysort` (the world viewport's draw calls attributable to `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors`, measured by hiding those groups in a dev harness and reading `RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` per viewport) exceeds about 300 on a release export at the default field or at the largest ladder field.
345	- **Go/no-go.** The fallback is built only if, in the spike room with the flag on versus off, **both** the world viewport's draw calls **and** frame CPU time are lower and the two pictures are bit-identical outside declared animating-source rectangles; otherwise it is withdrawn and the Pipeline's per-field draw caps (ADR-0008 § 7) apply. This ADR does not decide the measurement; SP-YSORT-1 and the Pipeline story do.
346	- **Shape if built.** A `ZBandMode.ROW_BANDED` variant of the same builder: the `Faces` and `Mounted` groups and the sprites become per-band `Node2D`s with `z_index = Z_WIN_LO + band` in the window 10 to 899 (`band = floor(sort_y / BAND_H) - band_0`, `BAND_H` the wall footprint depth, `band_0` from the union rectangle of every body drawn, recomputed on dock, weld and detach), with `Caps` and `Dust` moving to 900 and 910. Dependents are unaffected because they use band names; the largest value (910) is inside the default light range (V6). `diag.zband_overflow` and `diag.zband_negative` stay as the GDD defines them.

399	### Implementation Guidelines
400	- **Must** keep `World` and every `BodyRoot` `y_sort_enabled = true` and translation only; **must never** make a body root non-sorting, rotate, scale or skew it, or write its position anywhere but `Placement.put`.
401	- **Must** set a layer's `y_sort_origin` at the **layer** with `TileData.y_sort_origin = 0`, from the cell-centre formula of § 3.2; **must never** copy "24" from the GDD text without the cell height.
402	- **Must** use exactly one `TileSetAtlasSource` per `TileSet`, one `TileSet` per `(atlas_set, layer_kind)`, and preload them in `BOOTING`; **must never** `load()` or build a `TileSet` inside stage `PROJECT`.
403	- **Must** build under `Staging` (in the tree, hidden) and commit on the last unit; **must never** leave a half-built section visible, and **must never** build into a body root directly from the Layout projector.
404	- **Must** move nodes only with `SceneMove.to`; **must never** call `Node.reparent` with one argument, and **must never** free a node another presenter attached.
405	- **Must** keep `PropsActors` and the sprites of `Mounted` in `(class_rank, entity_id)` order through `SortedLayer`; **must never** tie-break by `x`, by creation order or by tree luck, and **must never** accept a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)`.
406	- **Must** compute `entity_id` only through `EntityId.pack` with a name from `EntityNs`; **must never** persist an `entity_id`, use a block-local id as one, or add a namespace byte in code outside `entity_ns.gd`.
407	- **Must** write `z_index` only in the group builder from `ZBand` names; **must never** write a z number or a `y_sort_enabled` value on a node outside the group and layer builders.
408	- **Must** publish `CameraLimits` in stage `PROJECT` and leave `Camera2D.limit_*` untouched; **must never** create a `Camera2D` under any body root.
409	- **Must** count work in units and respect `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` from the frozen `LayoutTuning` table; **must never** hold a literal for it in code.
410	- **Must** build bead, jamb, leaf, plate and scar sprites unchunked in the frame the weld notification is processed; **must never** chunk a socket-state change.
411	- **Must** keep all projector scripts in `src/presentation/projector/` (and the packing helpers in `src/shared/`); **must never** name `Node2D`, `TileMapLayer` or `Sprite2D` under `src/sim/`.
412	- **Should** make every projector class constructible with stub views so the audit tests run without a scene tree where the logic is pure (`DoorSort`, `InteriorDrawRule`, the limits union, the namespace packing).

414	## Alternatives Considered
415	
416	### Alternative 1: Option B, one Y-sort node and no per-body roots
417	- **Description**: Every section's nodes keep one parent under a single Y-sort node; each section's position is driven from the body's pose plus `section_offset` every tick, so a weld changes an offset and never a parent (LY-31 option B, tried first by the spike).
418	- **Pros**: no reparent at all; the PR-5 "ONE Y-sort `Node2D`" is literal; a weld is a data change.
419	- **Cons**: its only advantage was keeping one sort scope, which nested `y_sort_enabled` nodes already give (V2). It also moves every section node and every sprite, not one root, whenever a body's canvas offset changes; it needs a per-node body-offset add in every Presenter (an actor then needs its body's offset on every `Placement.put`), which spreads body knowledge into every presenter; BDY-33's per-body root and AC-BDY-92 would be rewritten; and the freed-root, node-count and "the root disappears after a weld" checks lose their meaning.
420	- **Rejection Reason**: The premise (single scope needs a single parent) is false on 4.7.2 by probe, and B costs more writes and more coupling for no gain. Kept as a recorded comparison for SP-YSORT-1, not as a fallback.
421	
422	### Alternative 2: Band-first (class layers at world level, per-body translation sub-roots)
423	- **Description**: `World` holds the band groups; each band group holds one translation sub-root per body, so equal keys across bodies resolve by class rank everywhere.
424	- **Pros**: cross-body equal-key ties follow the contract exactly; PR-5's "ONE Y-sort node" stays closest to literal.
425	- **Cons**: the body offset is written once per band per body per frame (five to seven writes, mostly skipped by `Placement.put`); "one per-body root" in BDY-33 and TR-shipbody-032 becomes seven sub-roots that must be created, ordered and freed together; a weld must move sub-roots in every band; the visibility rule (WM-19) must toggle seven nodes.
426	- **Rejection Reason**: It buys exactness only in the docked-seam equal-key corner (§ 3.4) at the price of the registered "one root per body" shape. If SP-YSORT-1 observes a visible cross-body flip, this is the first remedy; the `BodyScenes` facade hides which shape is underneath, so the change would be local.
427	
428	### Alternative 3: One `TileMapLayer` per body (sections merged)
429	- **Description**: A single tile map per layer kind per body, cells in body-frame coordinates.
430	- **Pros**: fewer nodes; one `update_internals` per body.
431	- **Cons**: impossible on the 24 px grid: welded sections can be offset by half a 48 px tile (the registry's MVP offset is 14.5 tiles), so cells cannot align; a salvage or discard rebuilds the whole body; the maintained and `_worn` atlases would share a layer, and two atlas sources in one layer cost 440 draw calls against 1 (V8).
432	- **Rejection Reason**: Does not fit the geometry and costs draws. Per-section layers cost a few extra nodes (V9: 75 us to reparent one).
433	
434	### Alternative 4: Rebuild the body's scene on every weld and cut
435	- **Description**: Free the moved sections' nodes and rebuild them under the new root through the same chunked path as a restore.
436	- **Pros**: one code path; the scene is always a fresh function of the views.
437	- **Cons**: spends a chunked build on a change that moves geometry but does not alter it; the first frame after a weld may show a gap or a stale scene (the old set must keep drawing, so two sets exist); the bead's same-frame rule (TR-assembly-045) conflicts with chunking; allocations per weld rise; foreign attachments (trails, items) would be orphaned by the free and need re-attaching.
438	- **Rejection Reason**: Reparent and shift is cheaper and has no gap. The rebuild path is kept as the reference for restore and as the equivalence oracle (§ 7).
439	
440	### Alternative 5: `Node.reparent(parent)` with the default global-transform preservation
441	- **Description**: Let the engine rewrite the local position so the node stays visually still.
442	- **Pros**: no explicit shift arithmetic.
443	- **Cons**: the engine rewrites a float local position, bypassing `Placement.put`, and the shift is not the integer `frame_shift_px` Layout reports; TR-shipbody-032 forbids it by name; V5 shows the local position changes.
444	- **Rejection Reason**: Violates the single integer assignment point and the TR.
445	
446	### Alternative 6: Build the per-row z-band fallback at MVP
447	- **Description**: Wall faces, mounted items and sprites in world-anchored 24-row z bands from the start (PR-5 fallback as the default).
448	- **Pros**: removes any dependence on Y-sort batching behaviour.
449	- **Cons**: one `TileMapLayer` per band, sprites reparented at every band crossing, a union rectangle over all drawn bodies recomputed on dock, weld and detach, and the GDD itself says it is built only if it lowers both draw calls and CPU; V8 suggests the single sorted scope may already be cheap with one atlas per layer.
450	- **Rejection Reason**: Pays a certain complexity for a speculative gain; the go/no-go rule of § 10 stands.
451	
452	### Alternative 7: Tie-break by tree insertion order or by `x`
453	- **Description**: Let the engine's tie rule decide equal keys, or break ties by `x`.
454	- **Pros**: no ordering structure.
455	- **Cons**: tree order is not save-stable (a reload can reverse creation order); `x` makes an actor swap order with a prop as it walks along a row, which PR-5's acceptance forbids.
456	- **Rejection Reason**: Contradicts TR-pxl-006. The engine's tie rule is used, but only after `SortedLayer` has made the tree order equal the contract order.
457	
458	### Alternative 8: Non-sorting body roots
459	- **Description**: Only the groups are sorted; the body roots are plain translation nodes.
460	- **Pros**: matches "the cap layer is not a child of a Y-sort node" literally; each body is its own sort unit.
461	- **Cons**: a non-sorting intermediate sorts its subtree as a unit (V2): the two docked bodies would be ordered by root order alone, so a sprite of one body would draw over or under the other as a block, which is wrong at the seam.
462	- **Rejection Reason**: Breaks LY-31 exit criterion (1) across two bodies. The cap and floor lints are restated by band instead.
463	
464	### Alternative 9: The Layout projector parents directly under Body's root (no staging)
465	- **Description**: LY-31's text: Layout's PROJECTOR parents its section nodes under Body's root.
466	- **Pros**: no handoff object.
467	- **Cons**: ADR-0009 registers the layout projector before `body.projector`, so the root may not exist yet for a new body; reversing the order would alter ADR-0009 and the occluder builder's dependency; a half-built section would be visible under a live root.
468	- **Rejection Reason**: The staging handoff keeps ADR-0009's order and gives atomic commits.
469	
470	## Consequences
471	
472	### Positive
473	- The weld and cut frames do work proportional to nodes moved, with no tile build and no gap; the bead appears in the first frame.
474	- One merged sort scope, probed, keeps PR-5's draw order across docked bodies without a special case.
475	- `entity_id` is a pure function of persisted ids, so draw order is stable across save and reload; the namespace table closes Layout OQ-33 and the Pipeline's open registration.
476	- Foreign presenters (Trail, Avatar, Interaction, Horror) get one attach API, so reparenting on `BODY_TRANSFER` is uniform and no presenter writes a z number.
477	- Per-section layers localise rebuilds, free a departed destination cleanly and respect the 24 px grid.
478	- The camera-limits path is a plain integer value read in the same frame; ADR-0009 OQ-C and OQ-I are closed on the PROJECTOR side.
479	
480	### Negative
481	- Several GDD texts need rewording (§ GDD Sync): the wall-face `y_sort_origin == 24` lint, the "cap layer is not a child of the Y-sort node" lint, BDY-33 (d) and LY-31's default shape.
482	- Cross-body equal-key ties follow body order, not the comparator (§ 3.4).
483	- `SortedLayer` costs O(n) `move_child` calls on a merge and a binary search per insert; fine at the MVP's hundreds of nodes, a measured assumption on Deck.
484	- The projector depends on reads that other ADRs have not yet published (`ProjectionSet`, the docked set, the `JAMB` ordinal, the `area_max` invariant); each is listed.
485	- A y-sorted `TileMapLayer` costs 0.39 ms to update 453 cells on the dev machine (V9), against 13 us unsorted; acceptable margin on a desktop, unproven on Deck.
486	
487	## Risks
488	- **R1: Nested-sort and tie behaviour differs on a release export, on a 4.7 patch release, or under the project's pinned Vulkan Forward+ at scale.** The probes ran on the editor binary on one GPU. Mitigation: SP-YSORT-1 reruns V1 to V4 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release exports; the tree-walk test and `PJT-01` keep the shape; Alternative 2 is the local fallback for cross-body order.
489	- **R2: The tile key formula (V3) is relied on and undocumented in the pinned reference.** Mitigation: a boot self-test builds a two-cell fixture and reads back the order; a mismatch fails boot with `PJT_TILE_KEY_FORMULA`; the formula is recorded in the registry so a patch-release change is a one-line fix.
490	- **R3: Cross-body equal-key flip at the docked seam (§ 3.4).** Mitigation: ordered by `body_id`; recorded in SP-YSORT-1; remedy Alternative 2.
491	- **R4: `D_ysort` exceeds the budget with real art (96 px faces break texture runs per row).** Mitigation: the § 10 rule; per-field draw caps in ADR-0008 § 7; the fallback is specified.
492	- **R5: The weld frame or an arrival exceeds budget on Deck.** Mitigation: the unit is data (`BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`), the weld does no tile work, and a hitch is bounded by `WELD_FRAME_HITCH_MAX_MS`; a second ladder rung is to move the shift of far sprites into the next frame, which the equal-key rule tolerates only within a body.
493	- **R6: A presenter attaches a node and frees it behind the projector's back.** Mitigation: `is_instance_valid` sweep, `PJT_ATTACH_DEAD` counter, lint `PJT-06` on `queue_free` of an attached node.
494	- **R7: The `ProjectionSet` or docked inputs are not published as assumed (ADR-0026).** Mitigation: a default implementation uses the avatar's body only and logs; Open Questions OQ-A and OQ-B.
495	- **R8: Wall cell width and wall tile art are not specified.** The sort key does not depend on cell width, but the tile pitch on the x axis must hold 24 px footprints for side walls. Mitigation: routed to the asset spec; Open Question OQ-D.
496	- **R9: Orphan noise.** A staged subtree outside the tree counts as orphans (V7). Mitigation: `Staging` is in the tree and hidden.
497	- **R10: Float32 exactness of body offsets.** Offsets are bounded by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (ADR-0015); the release-export probe is ADR-0008's.

537	## Performance Implications
538	- **CPU**: steady state, stage `PROJECT` does nothing but skipped `Placement.put` calls for body roots whose offset is unchanged and a dirty check; proposal 0.1 ms P99. A weld does O(nodes moved) work (reparent, shift, merge) plus a handful of sprite builds; a cut is the mirror; a build or arrival is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)` frames of at most one budget of units. Dev-machine margin (V9) is far below the 8 ms working threshold; release-export and Deck figures are UNVERIFIED.
539	- **Memory**: the MVP world's tiles and sprites are a few hundred nodes; a staged rebuild holds a second set of one section transiently; `TileSet` and atlas textures are shared across sections of the same atlas set. No per-frame allocation in steady state (CNT counters, ADR-0010).
540	- **Load Time**: preloading `TileSet`s and sheets happens in `BOOTING`, not in stage 0; an arrival builds the destination in the frames counted above under the black plate.
541	- **Network**: none at MVP; the projector is a local derived object (REPLICATION is dormant until VS-B).

546	## Validation Criteria
547	- **Order (auto, headless where pure):** `SortedLayer` property test: random inserts and merges give `(class_rank, entity_id)` order; the order is identical on 10 runs and after a rebuild that reverses creation order (PR-5 acceptance; AC-123 (b) within one body); a duplicate id is refused and counted.
548	- **Key formula (auto, windowed):** boot self-test of the tile key formula (R2); the PR-5 example (footprint rows 240 to 264, key 264; an actor at 232 sorts before, at 264 after) on the real layers.
549	- **Weld, cut, pod (integration with a scene harness, AC-BDY-92, AC-BDY-92b):** exactly one root per live body; after a weld the absorbed root is gone and node count equals the pre-weld count minus one with `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` flat; the Presenter's parent is the destination `PropsActors` in the same tick; draw order for an actor one pixel south and north of a wall edge before, on and after each transfer is unchanged.
550	- **Equivalence (auto):** a scripted weld, cut and pod sequence through an incremental projector and a fresh one fed `ALL` give equal `rebuild_signature()` (AC-121: the multiset of `(entity_id, kind_ordinal, position, size)` equals a live build).
551	- **No forbidden classes (auto, AC-122):** zero `CollisionShape2D`, `CollisionPolygon2D`, tile-set physics layer, `NavigationRegion2D`, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`; no `Camera2D` anywhere under `World`; no `Camera2D.limit_*` write.
552	- **Limits (auto):** the rectangle equals the union formula for one, two and three sections, grows north by `LIMITS_NORTH_OVERHANG`, is republished on weld, cut, load and `BODY_TRANSFER`, and the solver consumes it in the same frame.
553	- **Build rate (auto + perf):** the arrival scene builds in exactly `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)` frames with `U` counted from real `build_section` output; `ARRIVE_SCENE_LATE` fires when the latch is false at `DERELICT_LOADED`; the simulation tick count is unchanged by a late projector.
554	- **Atlas (auto, BOOT):** every catalog template has one `atlas_map` row; every `TileSet` has exactly one atlas source; no Layout field mentions wear.
555	- **Performance (perf, release export, RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK):** weld frame P99 at most the 8 ms working threshold over 100 welds; steady-state stage-0 proposal; `D_ysort` reported per viewport with the fallback trigger of § 10.
556	- **Lint pack `PJT-01` to `PJT-10` (ADR-0010 owns the tool and the tier; proposed here):** `PJT-01` body roots and `World` are `y_sort_enabled`, translation only (tree walk); `PJT-02` the group set and order under a body root; `PJT-03` `z_index` written only in the group builder, no z literal; `PJT-04` no one-argument `.reparent(`, parent changes only through `SceneMove`; `PJT-05` no `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`, collision or navigation class in `src/presentation/projector/`; `PJT-06` no `queue_free`/`free` of an attached node by its owner without `detach`; `PJT-07` `Camera2D` absent under `World`, no `limit_` write; `PJT-08` `EntityId.pack` takes a name from `EntityNs`, never a literal; `PJT-09` no `load(` / `preload(` inside a `present` callable; `PJT-10` every `TileSet` built by `TileSetCache` has one atlas source.

46:- **Half-open input boxes, occupied-span output** (LY-12 b): every box passed in is `[ax0, ax1) x [ay0, ay1)`; every rect handed out is `(x0, y0, x1 - 1, y1 - 1)`. Output is in the **body frame** and in ascending `rect_key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` (D.9); the key is 64-bit.
92:        |                                            section_rects_into(section_id, mask, out)
102:**One structure, three consumers' views.** For every LIVE body `RectIndex` owns one `BodyGrid`. Its core is a **row table** with one row per rect slot of every section on the body: every static rect, every door-leaf slot and every socket PLATE/JAMB slot of ADR-0013 § 5, **including slots that are currently inactive or zero-length** (they keep their row, exactly as they keep their `idx`). `rects_in` and `solid_in` are not two indexes: they are **two flag masks over this one table** (`OCCLUDES_LIGHT` and `SOLID`, registry `layout_rect_flags`). A third reader, the PROJECTOR, reads the same rows through `section_rects_into` (§ 5). That single table is what TR-section-011 means by "one rect set": no consumer has a private copy to drift, and no query has a perceived or phantom variant.
104:**Rows are in key order by construction.** The table is built by walking the body's sections in ascending `section_id` (`sections_of(body_id)` already answers ascending) and, inside a section, `idx` ascending (`0 .. rect_count() - 1`). Because `rect_key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` and `idx < RECT_KEY_STRIDE`, **row order is key order**: row `r < s` implies `key[r] < key[s]`, keys are strictly ascending and unique, and no sort is ever needed to produce ascending-key output. This is a rule, not an accident of one probe: the build asserts it (a debug diagnostic `rows_not_ascending`) and a unit test walks every fixture body.
121:**Flag masks.** `RectFlags` (bit names from the registry; the bit values and the file are ADR-0013's Layout epic, § Cross-ADR assumptions): `SolidQuery.solid_in` uses `RectFlags.SOLID`; `OccluderSource.rects_in` uses `RectFlags.OCCLUDES_LIGHT`; `section_rects_into` takes the caller's mask. Actors and horrors have no row (Layout holds no actor), so **they can never occlude or block through this index** (TR-light-035, TR-emitter-018 c); a prop is in the OCCLUDES_LIGHT set only when its template flags say so (LY-7).
187:@abstract func section_rects_into(section_id: int, mask: int, out: QueryBuffer) -> int   # bulk read for builders; § below
199:**`section_rects_into(section_id, mask, out)`** is the bulk read the occluder builder and the PROJECTOR need and that no GDD named: all rows of one section whose flags intersect `mask` and whose current extent is non-empty, in the body frame, ascending key, same record layout. It walks the section's contiguous row block (no grid, no stamp), so its cost is linear in the section's rect count and it is meant for change-driven rebuilds, not per-frame polling. It lets Lighting rebuild "section s" without guessing a bounding box for `rects_in` (which would also return a neighbouring section's abutting rects) and lets the PROJECTOR size a door-leaf sprite from the same row the simulation tests, which is the "leaf sprite extent equals the leaf rect" half of TR-section-013 and the "drawing" leg of TR-section-011. Unknown or discarded section: returns 0 with `out.status = UNKNOWN_SECTION`.
344:- **Must** return an empty or inverted box as 0 with `status = EMPTY_BOX`, an unknown body as 0 with `status = UNKNOWN_BODY` and an unknown section from `section_rects_into` as 0 with `UNKNOWN_SECTION`; **must never** raise a fault or throw for any of them, and callers **must** read `status` when "no rectangles" and "no such body" mean different things (Horror, TR-horror-031).
469:- **R9 Insertion cost on very large boxes** (hundreds of results). Mitigation: rung 4; no consumer in the MVP queries such a box through the grid (Lighting uses `section_rects_into`).

230:**Weld offset (D.6, TR-section-021).** `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b`, where `a` is the **survivor-side** socket and `b` the absorbed-side socket, assigned **by body, never by argument order**: the body with the **lower `body_id`** survives (the older body; the home ship in the MVP). `attach_section` re-labels the two arguments internally, so `attach_section(x, y, ...)` and `attach_section(y, x, ...)` produce the same survivor, the same `offset_b`, the same `frame_shift_px`, and a **byte-identical** `layout.state`: the `welds[]` row always records the survivor-side section and socket as `section_a`/`socket_a` (canonicalisation). `weld_math.gd` is a pure module of integer helpers (`survivor_of`, `offset_b`, `frame_shift`) with no state, which `weld_offset(...)` (the pure read), `can_attach` and LM2 all call, so prediction and apply cannot drift.
234:**LM2 effects, in order** (all inside the caller's single P2 apply, after the Graph's `weld_join`): append the `welds[]` row (`ACTIVE`); upsert both socket rows to `WELDED(seam_id)` keeping ascending order; shift every section of the absorbed body by `frame_shift_px = offset_b - offset_b_old` and move it to the survivor `body_id`; mark the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switch the PLATE/JAMB/LEAF slots of both sockets (§ 6); seed each newly active LEAF **closed** with its last-projected cache (§ 8); rebuild the affected broadphase handles (ADR-0014); bump `static_version` and `version` of **every section whose socket state changed (including the host section that does not move) and every moved section**; stamp `changed_region` (REGION for the two socket-host sections, FRAME for the other moved sections); cache the mated hatch's opening ids from `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]` into `opening_leaves`; mark `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>` and `SEC/<id>` for each affected section (5 keys for the MVP weld of two single-section bodies). The returned `AttachResult` carries `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}`; `body_of` of every moved section is the survivor in the same apply and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick.
236:**LM3 and the detach re-base (D.12).** After the Graph's `cut_detach`, LM3 marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` (keeping `seam_id`); then **enumerates the connected components of the `ACTIVE` weld forest minus the cut seam, in ascending `section_id`**. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other receives a new `body_id` from `next_body_id`, its `origin_section_id` is `m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component, and its offsets are re-based by `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` (`offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) - frame_shift`). content.text: Now ADR Dependencies and Ordering Note.

input.old_string: **Depends On** | ADR-0009 (PROJECTOR class rights, stage `PROJECT` and its registration order, `PresenterDescriptor`, `Placement`, chunked rebuild, the single-chunk in-reach rule for Lighting's occluder builder only; Proposed), ADR-0008 (world viewport, body frame as the canvas, `CameraSolver`, z-band names, draw-call table, `RenderLayout`; Proposed),
input.new_string: **Depends On** | ADR-0009 (PROJECTOR class rights, stage `PROJECT` and its registration order, `PresenterDescriptor`, `Placement`, chunked rebuild, the single-chunk in-reach rule for Lighting's occluder builder only; Proposed). **Foundation amendments this ADR relies on (CT-34, CT-35, CT-55, requested of ADR-0009, not yet applied):** (i) the Layout projector and `body.projector` are one PROJECTOR pair with a declared same-stage handoff object (`SectionScene`), `body.projector` declaring `after: [layout_projector]`; (ii) `BodyScenes` is a named **mutation facade** (`attach`, `attach_presenter`, `attach_light`, `detach`, `rebind` only; never a getter of private state) that later-stage presenters may call, an exception to ADR-0009 § 1's "presentation never reads another presenter's private state"; (iii) the reparent wording is reworded so that `Node.reparent(parent, false)` through `SceneMove` is the sanctioned primitive (ADR-0009 said "without `Node.reparent`"); (iv) § 2 of ADR-0009 ("a PROJECTOR answering `ALL` keeps drawing the last complete state") is satisfied for a restore by ADR-0008's load hold, which is held until `ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()`, not by keeping old roots. ADR-0008 (world viewport, body frame as the canvas, `CameraSolver`, z-band names, draw-call table, `RenderLayout`, `rect_eff`, the clamp order, the load hold; Proposed),

input.old_string: ADR-0015 (`BodyView` `world` and `world_prev`, `BODY_TRANSFER` records, the canvas-offset formula it hands to this ADR, the 2^22 and 2^24 bounds; Proposed draft), ADR-0004
input.new_string: ADR-0015 (`BodyView` `world` and `world_prev`, `BODY_TRANSFER` records, the canvas-offset formula it hands to this ADR, `BODY_COORD_LIMIT` (at most 2^24, restore-checked) and the canvas bound `|world_a - world_b| + |pos| < 2^23` under `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX` (otherwise `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` is lowered), CT-24; Proposed draft), ADR-0007 (frozen catalogs, the `LayoutTuning` table, and the new `presentation` data domain this ADR introduces, `atlas_map.json`: an amendment request, hence a hard dependency, CT-57; Proposed), ADR-0004

input.old_string: **Soft:** ADR-0014 (the rect table the sprites are built from, `section_rects_into`; Proposed draft), ADR-0007 (frozen catalogs, the `LayoutTuning` table, a new `presentation` data domain; Proposed), ADR-0011
input.new_string: **Soft:** ADR-0014 (the rect table the sprites are built from: `section_rects_into(section_id, mask, out)` in the body frame as occupied spans, and `OccluderSource.idx_of_key(key)`, CT-18; Proposed draft), ADR-0011

input.old_string: **This ADR stays Proposed. Acceptance requires** SP-YSORT-1 to pass the five LY-31 exit criteria as remapped in § 11 on a release export, ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 Accepted, and the namespace table of § 4 agreed by the owners of the five publishers.
input.new_string: **This ADR stays Proposed. Acceptance requires** SP-YSORT-1 to pass the five LY-31 exit criteria as remapped in § 11 on a release export, and ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 Accepted (with the amendments listed under Depends On). The namespace table of § 4 is **not** an acceptance condition (T6): the publishers' ADRs (ADR-0020, ADR-0023, ADR-0026, ADR-0027, the Trail ADR) are later tiers that list this ADR as an input, so the table is registered here as **append-only with a golden test**; a later ADR adopts its byte or requests an append, and never renumbers.

class_name SortedLayer extends RefCounted
## Wraps one sorted group node. Sprite children are kept in ascending (class_rank, entity_id); the parallel arrays hold the order.
## The group's TileMapLayer children are a PREFIX of its child list (LayerOrder below); every child index here is `layers.count() + array index`.

func merge_from(other: SortedLayer) -> void                           ## one pass: both inputs are sorted, so compute final indices (base layers.count()), then move_child once per node
func count() -> int

# src/presentation/projector/layer_order.gd
class_name LayerOrder extends RefCounted
## The TileMapLayers of one band group, kept as the first children in ascending section_id. Used for all four layer-bearing groups (Floor, Faces, Mounted, Caps).
var _layers: Array[TileMapLayer]
var _sid: PackedInt32Array
func add(layer: TileMapLayer, section_id: int) -> void   ## add_child (or after SceneMove.to), then move_child(layer, rank among layers)
func remove(layer: TileMapLayer) -> void                 ## does not free
func count() -> int
```
`insert` finds the index by binary search over `(rank, eid)`, calls `add_child` and then `move_child(node, layers.count() + index)`; a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)` is refused (counted as `diag.sort_id_collision`, which must stay zero) rather than silently ordered by tree position. `merge_from` serves the weld: the survivor's and the absorbed body's `PropsActors` are each already sorted, so the merged order is one linear pass followed by one `move_child` per node (V9: 100 moves cost 0.05 ms on the dev machine).

**The order guarantee covers TileMapLayer children too (E2, T4).** `reparent(p, false)` appends the moved node as the **last** child (V5), so after a weld a moved section's layers would sit after the existing sprites and `move_child` indexes in `SortedLayer`'s array would be off by the number of layer children; and two sections' layers at an equal key would tie by weld history, not by `section_id`, which changes after a save and reload (a reload rebuilds in ascending `section_id`). The **LayerOrder step** therefore runs in `SceneMove`'s caller (`body.projector`) after every mount, move and removal: the group's `TileMapLayer`s are `move_child`-ed to the front, ordered by ascending `section_id`, and `SortedLayer`'s index base is `layers.count()` (the tile layers are a prefix of the child list, then the sprites). In `Mounted` this realises "rank-1 tiles first, then rank-1 sprites"; in `Floor`, `Faces` and `Caps` it makes cross-section layer order a function of the persisted `section_id`. Ties **inside** one layer are the engine's own and are deterministic: same-row cells tie by x, higher x on top, independent of `set_cell` order and unchanged by a reparent (V10, review probe). **Tiles carry no `entity_id`**; the cross-layer and layer-versus-sprite ties resolve by `section_id` (layers) and then `(class_rank, entity_id)` (sprites), never by mount order. `ProjectorAudit` checks this with a tree walk (`PJT-02`: layers precede sprites in every group, layers ascending by `section_id`) and `rebuild_signature()` includes the **ordered child list per group** (§ 7).

content.thinking: I'm now working through the Sprites section, the Two projectors example, and the SectionScene class, drafting replacement content for each.

input.old_string:
are built from the rect table (`section_rects_into`, ADR-0014: rows carry `idx`, flags and the current extent) and the template's visual rows (kit-piece ids and layers, the `visual_hash` part of the frozen template, ADR-0013 § 4), not from tiles. Each carries `entity_id = EntityId.pack(EntityNs.LAYOUT, layout_local(section_id, kind_ordinal, idx))` and its class rank from § 4. Socket-state sprites (PLATE, JAMB, LEAF, bead, scar) are rebuilt from `welds[]` and the socket rows on `SEC`, `SEAM` and `LEAF` keys.

**Two projectors, one handoff.** The Layout projector builds and owns a `SectionScene` per live section; `body.projector` owns bodies and roots and mounts scenes. ADR-0009 registers the layout projector first, then `body.projector`, which would force a body root to exist before the Layout projector can parent into it; that is avoided by having the Layout projector build **into the hidden `Staging` holder** and never into a body root. A `SectionScene` exposes `mount(body_root_set, section_offset)` and `unmount()` that only `body.projector` calls; when the Layout projector later swaps a rebuilt layer it asks the scene to `swap_in`, and the scene replaces its node under whatever parent it is currently mounted on. The registration order of ADR-0009 is therefore unchanged and sufficient.
input.new_string:
are built from the rect table and the template's visual rows (kit-piece ids and layers, the `visual_hash` part of the frozen template, ADR-0013 § 4), not from tiles. Each carries `entity_id = EntityId.pack(EntityNs.LAYOUT, layout_local(section_id, kind_ordinal, idx))` and its class rank from § 4. Socket-state sprites (PLATE, JAMB, LEAF, bead, scar) are rebuilt from `welds[]` and the socket rows on `SEC`, `SEAM` and `LEAF` keys.

**The rect read and the frame rule (T1, ruling CT-18).** The projector calls ADR-0014's real signature, `section_rects_into(section_id, mask, out)` (`mask` is the caller's `RectFlags` mask). Rows are in the **body frame** and are **occupied spans**: `(x0, y0, x1 - 1, y1 - 1)`, so a sprite's width is `span + 1` (using the span as a half-open rect would leave every sprite 1 px short and break TR-section-013); each row carries `key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` and a flags byte, and `idx = OccluderSource.idx_of_key(key)` (ADR-0014 adds the read because `/` and `%` are banned outside `IntMath`; `idx` is not a column). A row whose current extent is empty is omitted, so the consumer **hides** that sprite. The kind (JAMB, PLATE, LEAF and so on) is derived from the reserved `idx` ranges of ADR-0013 § 5. **Each `SectionScene` converts to section-local px once, at build, by subtracting `section_offset_x/_y(section_id)`, and stores every sprite's section-local rect** (`sprite_local`: four ints per sprite). Thereafter a sprite's body-frame position is **never** moved by adding a delta: on build, mount, weld, cut and re-base, `body.projector` writes `position = section_offset(section_id) + local_origin` through `Placement.put`, **recomputed from the current offset** (`local_origin` from the stored local rect and the placement rule of § 3.1). A sprite built before a weld and one built in the same frame as the weld therefore get the same position as a fresh `ALL` build. A **staged** scene whose section received a `BODY` or `SEC` key during its build recomputes every position at commit, so a chunked build that straddles a weld, cut or re-base cannot commit sprites in the old frame.

**Two projectors, one handoff (rulings CT-34, CT-55).** The two PROJECTOR subscribers are one pair with a declared same-stage handoff object, the `SectionScene` (a Foundation amendment to ADR-0009 § 1, listed under Depends On): `LayoutProjector` registers `PresenterDescriptor(name = &"layout_projector", stage = PROJECT, reads = [], after = [])` and `BodyProjector` registers `(name = &"body_projector", stage = PROJECT, reads = [], after = [&"layout_projector"])` (`reads` lists earlier stages, and the handoff is same-stage, hence the amendment rather than a `reads` entry). **The rule:** the Layout projector creates nodes **only in `Staging` or through `SectionScene` methods**; **all parenting and `SortedLayer` insertion under a body root goes through `body.projector`**, which may be invoked through the `SectionScene`. ADR-0009 registers the layout projector first, then `body.projector`, which would force a body root to exist before the Layout projector could parent into it; that is avoided by having the Layout projector build **into the hidden `Staging` holder** and never into a body root. A `SectionScene` exposes `mount(...)`, `unmount()`, `swap_in(...)` and `add_sprite(...)` and `body.projector` executes them: when the Layout projector builds a replacement layer or a new socket-state sprite for a scene that is already mounted, it hands it to the scene (`stage_swap`, `add_sprite` queue the node in `Staging`), and `body.projector`, which runs second in the same stage-0 pass, performs the parenting, the `LayerOrder`/`SortedLayer` insertion and the position write in its own pass. The registration order of ADR-0009 is therefore unchanged and sufficient.

input.old_string: The number of frames for a build of `U` units is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)`, plus one if the final commit needs its own `present`.
input.new_string: The number of frames for a build of `U` units is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)`, plus one if the final commit needs its own `present`. **`U` counts data work only.** `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` bounds `set_cell` and node configuration; it does **not** bound the engine's canvas-item build of a layer, which happens in one unchunked deferred burst when a layer first becomes visible in the tree, i.e. at mount (V10 f). That burst is the **mount term `R_mount`** (about 0.9 us per cell on the dev machine, unmeasured for Deck). It is declared **unchunked and counted in frames, not in units**: scenes are mounted **one scene per `present` call** in ascending `section_id`, so an arrival or restore of `S` scenes takes `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME) + S` frames at most (the mounts may overlap the tail of the data build), and `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` is sized to that count (GDD Sync). The per-scene burst is bounded by that scene's cell count and is measured by SP-YSORT-1 (V9').
