input.old_string: The number of frames for a build of `U` units is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)`, plus one if the final commit needs its own `present`.
input.new_string: The number of frames for a build of `U` units is `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)`, plus one if the final commit needs its own `present`. **`U` counts data work only.** `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` bounds `set_cell` and node configuration; it does **not** bound the engine's canvas-item build of a layer, which happens in one unchunked deferred burst when a layer first becomes visible in the tree, i.e. at mount (V10 f). That burst is the **mount term `R_mount`** (about 0.9 us per cell on the dev machine, unmeasured for Deck). It is declared **unchunked and counted in frames, not in units**: scenes are mounted **one scene per `present` call** in ascending `section_id`, so an arrival or restore of `S` scenes takes `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME) + S` frames at most (the mounts may overlap the tail of the data build), and `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` is sized to that count (GDD Sync). The per-scene burst is bounded by that scene's cell count and is measured by SP-YSORT-1 (V9').

input.old_string: **Staging and atomic commit.** A new or rebuilt section builds under the `Staging` holder (in the tree, `visible = false`, so `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` stays flat, V7) and `complete` flips only on the last unit. `body.projector` mounts a scene only when `complete`, in one pass, so no frame draws half a section. A rebuild of an already mounted section (a salvage that changes its template-visible state) builds a second set in `Staging`, keeps drawing the old set until the last chunk, then swaps (`swap_in`) in one apply; the same "old complete state keeps drawing" rule ADR-0009 § 2 states for the PROJECTOR.
input.new_string: **Staging and atomic commit.** A new or rebuilt section builds under the `Staging` holder (in the tree, `visible = false`, so the orphan delta stays zero in the editor and debug runner, V7) and `complete` flips only on the last unit. **`Staging` is a data stage only:** the engine builds nothing for a layer that is not visible in the tree (V10 f), so staging does not pre-warm rendering and chunking does not hide the real build, which lands at mount. `body.projector` mounts a scene only when `complete`, in one pass, so no frame draws half a section (the mount's own rebuild is the unchunked burst `R_mount` of the work-unit paragraph above). A rebuild of an already mounted section (a salvage that changes its template-visible state) builds a second set in `Staging`, keeps drawing the old set until the last chunk, then swaps (`swap_in`, executed by `body.projector`) in one apply; the same "old complete state keeps drawing" rule ADR-0009 § 2 states for the PROJECTOR. For a **restore, new game or `ALL`** the rule is satisfied differently (§ 7): the roots are rebuilt under ADR-0008's load hold, which is held until `ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()`, so no partial interior is ever visible.

input.old_string: **What is not chunked.** Anything a weld or cut needs in the first frame: reparenting and shifting nodes (§ 7), the socket-state sprites (bead, jambs, leaf, plate, scar: a handful of sprites, not tiles), root creation and freeing, the limits publish.
input.new_string: **What is not chunked.** Anything a weld or cut needs in the first frame: reparenting nodes and recomputing their positions (§ 7), the engine's deferred rebuild of the reparented layers (`R_weld`, charged to the weld budget), the socket-state sprites (bead, jambs, leaf, plate, scar: a handful of sprites, not tiles), root creation and freeing, a `BodyRoot.visible` flip (`R_flip`, § 8), the limits publish.

content.thinking: Now I'm moving to rewrite section 7, starting with the Decision paragraph and working through the Weld steps, Cut, Pod hop, and Restore pieces one at a time.

input.old_string: **Decision.** On a weld or cut the projector **moves** the affected sections' existing nodes to their new body root and shifts their positions by the Layout-reported `frame_shift_px`; it **rebuilds no tile**. Rebuilding the whole destination scene on every weld was rejected (Alternative 4): it spends a chunked build, shows a frame boundary, makes two code paths for the same tree anyway, and gives no benefit because a moved section's geometry does not change.
input.new_string: **Decision.** On a weld or cut the projector **moves** the affected sections' existing nodes to their new body root and recomputes their positions from the current `section_offset` (§ 5); it **re-authors no tile** (no `set_cell`, no chunked build). It does not follow that nothing is rebuilt: on 4.7.2 reparenting a `TileMapLayer` makes the engine rebuild every cell once, in the deferred internal update that follows (V10), so a weld costs about 0.9 us per cell per moved layer on the dev machine (453 sorted cells about 0.4 ms), unchunked and unmeasured for Deck. That engine rebuild is the weld budget term `R_weld` (§ 11). Re-authoring the whole destination scene on every weld was rejected (Alternative 4): it spends a chunked build **and** the same engine rebuild, shows a frame boundary, makes two code paths for the same tree anyway, and gives no benefit because a moved section's geometry does not change. A zero-rebuild alternative (a permanent per-section parent, Alternative 10) is recorded as the remedy if `R_weld` is measured over budget.

input.old_string:
1. Reads the new `bodies[]` and `section_offset` of each section (Layout views). For every `SectionScene` whose `mounted_body_id` differs from `body_of(section_id)`, computes `delta = new_offset - mounted_off`, which equals the `frame_shift_px` of the weld for every moved section.
2. Moves the scene's four layer nodes to the matching group of the survivor root with `SceneMove.to`, and writes each layer's `position = new_offset` with `Placement.put`.

input.old_string: **Restore, new game, `ALL`.** `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` frees every scene and root and rebuilds from the views through the same build path (staged, chunked, atomic). `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so nothing interpolates across the break. A scripted weld, cut and pod sequence through an incrementally updated projector and a fresh projector fed `ALL` must give equal `rebuild_signature()` values (ADR-0009 § 2 safety net, mandatory here: the projector is the first key-level incremental presenter whose two paths differ in kind).
input.new_string:
**Restore, new game, `ALL` (CT-33).** `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` first runs the **parking step** (§ 7.2), then frees every scene and root, then rebuilds from the views through the same build path (staged, chunked, atomic, mounted one scene per `present`), and re-mounts each parked attachment when its body or section is mounted again. The roots are rebuilt **under the pipeline's load hold, which ADR-0008 releases only when `ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()`**: the interior is never drawn partially, which is the intent of ADR-0009 § 2 (keeping the old roots drawing was rejected: it does not cover a cold load, where no old roots exist). `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so nothing interpolates across the break. A scripted weld, cut and pod sequence through an incrementally updated projector and a fresh projector fed `ALL` must give equal `rebuild_signature()` values, **which include the ordered child list of every band group** (layers by `section_id`, then sprites by `(class_rank, entity_id)`, T4), compared as an ordered list and not as a multiset (the AC-121 multiset check alone cannot see an order difference). This is the ADR-0009 § 2 safety net, mandatory here: the projector is the first key-level incremental presenter whose two paths differ in kind.

**7.2 Parking foreign attachments (CT-33, T2).** Freeing a `BodyRoot` also frees every node attached under it, including the Avatar Presenter, Trail, Interaction, Horror and Suit nodes, which contradicts the rule that the projector never frees a node another presenter attached. So **before any root or scene is freed** (restore, `ALL`, a `ProjectionSet` exit, a dissolved or dead body), `body.projector` **parks** every foreign attachment of what is about to be freed in `Staging` with `SceneMove.to`, and **keeps its registration** `(body_id, section_id, rank, entity_id)`. When the attachment's body or section is mounted again, the projector re-mounts it into the correct group (`LayerOrder`/`SortedLayer` order restored; the owner rewrites an actor-following node's position in the same frame). For a parked attachment whose body or section **no longer exists** (a section discarded, a body dissolved or dead), the projector calls the attachment's declared `on_orphaned` notification (set at `attach`, a `Callable` taking the node), after which the owner decides to re-attach or free; a parked node with no owner response for a frame is counted `PJT_ATTACH_ORPHANED`, never freed by the projector. A parked node sits in the hidden `Staging` holder, which is in the tree, so it adds no orphan.

content.text: Now the 7.1 BodyScenes block.

input.old_string:
**7.1 The attach API (generalising `attach_presenter`).** Other presenters need a sanctioned way into the projector's tree so that reparent-on-weld is uniform:

```gdscript
# src/presentation/projector/body_scenes.gd : the facade body.projector exposes (RefCounted, injected at setup())
class_name BodyScenes extends RefCounted
const OK: int = 0
const ERR_UNKNOWN_BODY: int = -1
const ERR_DUPLICATE_ID: int = -2
const ERR_BAND_DENIED: int = -3          # the band is projector-only (Floor, Faces, Caps) or the rank does not fit the band
const ERR_NO_SECTION: int = -4           # a non-actor attachment must name its section
## Attach a node a presenter built. The projector parents it, orders it, shifts it on weld and cut, and never frees it.
func attach(body_id: int, band: int, node: Node2D, class_rank: int, entity_id: int, section_id: int) -> int
## Remove the attachment; the node is left alive and parentless (the owner frees or re-attaches it).
func detach(node: Node2D) -> void
## The Avatar Presenter's registration (BDY-33 (f)): band PropsActors, class rank 3, entity_id = pack(BODY, actor_id), section_id 0.
func attach_presenter(actor_id: int, node: Node2D) -> int
```
Allowed bands for foreign nodes: `Marks` (Trail floor marks), `Mounted` (Trail wall trails, rank 1), `PropsActors` (Interaction and Suit items rank 2, Body actors and Horror rigs rank 3, off-floor web pieces rank 2), `Dust` (particles). `Floor`, `Faces` and `Caps` are projector-only. A non-actor attachment must name its `section_id` so the projector can move it with its section on a weld or cut; an actor attachment is moved by its `BODY_TRANSFER` record. The projector sets the group's z; the owner never writes `z_index`, which is what makes "no trail uses z 0 or +20" structural. When a body root is freed its foreign children have already been moved out; an attached node that is freed by its owner is dropped from the layer's arrays on the next `is_instance_valid` sweep (counted `PJT_ATTACH_DEAD`).
input.new_string:
**7.1 The attach API (generalising `attach_presenter`).** Other presenters need a sanctioned way into the projector's tree so that reparent-on-weld is uniform. `BodyScenes` is declared a **mutation facade** under the ADR-0009 exception (CT-34): later-stage presenters (stages 2 to 7) may call exactly `attach`, `attach_presenter`, `attach_light`, `detach` and `rebind` on this stage-0 product, and it exposes **no getter of the projector's private state**:

```gdscript
# src/presentation/projector/body_scenes.gd : the facade body.projector exposes (RefCounted, injected at setup())
class_name BodyScenes extends RefCounted
const OK: int = 0
const ERR_UNKNOWN_BODY: int = -1
const ERR_DUPLICATE_ID: int = -2
const ERR_BAND_DENIED: int = -3          # the band is projector-only (Floor, Faces, Caps) or the rank does not fit the band
const ERR_NO_SECTION: int = -4           # a non-actor attachment must name its section
## Attach a node a presenter built. The projector parents it, orders it, moves it on weld and cut, parks it before any free, and never frees it.
## on_orphaned: called with the node when its body or section no longer exists (§ 7.2); the owner re-attaches or frees.
func attach(body_id: int, band: int, node: Node2D, class_rank: int, entity_id: int, section_id: int, on_orphaned: Callable = Callable()) -> int
## Remove the attachment; the node is left alive and parentless (the owner frees or re-attaches it).
func detach(node: Node2D) -> void
## The Avatar Presenter's registration (BDY-33 (f)): band PropsActors, class rank 3, entity_id = pack(BODY, actor_id), section_id 0.
func attach_presenter(actor_id: int, node: Node2D) -> int
## A beam or actor-following Light2D (ruling CT-32): parent is the translation-only BodyRoot of BodyView.body_of_actor(actor_id), not a band group;
## registered under EntityNs.LIGHTING with the seat's beam id. The projector creates no Light2D; it only parents the node the Lighting presenter built.
func attach_light(actor_id: int, beam_id: int, node: Node2D) -> int
## Re-register a non-actor attachment under another body and section (a mobile owner: Horror rig, mobile Suit or Interaction prop). The caller MUST call it
## in the same frame its owner's section changes (an obligation on ADR-0023, ADR-0020, ADR-0027); the projector moves the node with SceneMove.to,
## and the owner's next Placement.put must be written in the NEW body's frame.

input.new_string:
`world` is exterior-only and bounded by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`, so every offset is within `2^23` and exact in `float32` under ADR-0015's published bounds: `BODY_COORD_LIMIT` (at most 2^24, restore-checked, repeated in Layout's `can_attach`) and `|world_a - world_b| + |pos| < 2^23` under `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX`, otherwise `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` is lowered, CT-24). The avatar's body root is at (0, 0). A root whose offset did not change costs one skipped write.

**The BODY_TRANSFER pass (rulings CT-32, T7).** In stage 0, **before stage `AVATAR` (2)**, for each `BODY_TRANSFER` record `body.projector` reparents, in one pass and through `SceneMove` (`reparent(p, false)`), the actor's Presenter node **and every `LIGHTING` node of that actor** (keyed by the seat's beam id) to the translation-only `BodyRoot` of `BodyView.body_of_actor(actor)`. `reparent` would preserve the global transform by default (V5); `keep_global_transform = false` keeps the local position instead, and **the projector writes no actor-following node's position**: the owning presenter (stage `AVATAR` 2 or `LIGHTING` 6, both after stage 0) rewrites the position from `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y` in the same frame, before draw. A **dev assertion** (`projector_reparented_not_rewritten`, checked at the last presenter stage) requires that every node reparented this frame received an owner `Placement.put` before draw. The beam `Light2D`'s parent is therefore always `BodyRoot(body_of_actor(actor))` (ADR-0018 SHO-04 asserts it on every dev frame; ADR-0015 V8 is answered by this probe: `keep_global_transform` false, owner rewrites position). A mobile owner calls `BodyScenes.rebind` when its own section changes (§ 7.1).

**Visibility (WM-19, defence in depth).** `BodyRoot.visible = InteriorDrawRule.visible(b, avatar_body, ...)`: true for the avatar's body and for a body docked or welded to it; false for a body drawn only as an exterior silhouette (those are not this tree). The rule is a pure function with injected inputs so it is unit-testable; its docked input is a Web Map read (an assumption on ADR-0026). Hiding a root hides its subtree and its lights' occluders are Lighting's concern. **Decision: WM-19 uses `BodyRoot.visible`; the projection set does not free and rebuild on a flip.** Cost, per V10 (e): hiding costs 0 rebuilds, but **every false-to-true flip rebuilds every cell under that root** in one unchunked deferred burst (`R_flip`, about 0.9 us per cell on the dev machine, unmeasured for Deck), and a root first shown after being hidden pays a full build. Flips happen on dock, undock and arrival events, never per frame; each is charged to the arrival or dock budget and SP-YSORT-1 measures `R_flip` for the largest root (V9'). If `R_flip` is over budget the remedy is Alternative 10 together with retaining hidden scenes (OQ-F).

**The BODY_TRANSFER pass (rulings CT-32, T7).** In stage 0, **before stage `AVATAR` (2)**, for each `BODY_TRANSFER` record `body.projector` reparents, in one pass and through `SceneMove` (`reparent(p, false)`), the actor's Presenter node **and every `LIGHTING` node of that actor** (keyed by the seat's beam id) to the translation-only `BodyRoot` of `BodyView.body_of_actor(actor)`. `reparent` would preserve the global transform by default (V5); `keep_global_transform = false` keeps the local position instead, and **the projector writes no actor-following node's position**: the owning presenter (stage `AVATAR` 2 or `LIGHTING` 6, both after stage 0) rewrites the position from `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y` in the same frame, before draw. A **dev assertion** (`projector_reparented_not_rewritten`, checked at the last presenter stage) requires that every node reparented this frame received an owner `Placement.put` before draw. The beam `Light2D`'s parent is therefore always `BodyRoot(body_of_actor(actor))` (ADR-0018 SHO-04 asserts it on every dev frame; ADR-0015 V8 is answered by this probe: `keep_global_transform` false, owner rewrites position). A mobile owner calls `BodyScenes.rebind` when its own section changes (§ 7.1).

**Visibility (WM-19, defence in depth).** `BodyRoot.visible = InteriorDrawRule.visible(b, avatar_body, ...)`: true for the avatar's body and for a body docked or welded to it; false for a body drawn only as an exterior silhouette (those are not this tree). The rule is a pure function with injected inputs so it is unit-testable; its docked input is a Web Map read (an assumption on ADR-0026). Hiding a root hides its subtree and its lights' occluders are Lighting's concern. **Decision: WM-19 uses `BodyRoot.visible`; the projection set does not free and rebuild on a flip.** Cost, per V10 (e): hiding costs 0 rebuilds, but **every false-to-true flip rebuilds every cell under that root** in one unchunked deferred burst (`R_flip`, about 0.9 us per cell on the dev machine, unmeasured for Deck), and a root first shown after being hidden pays a full build. Flips happen on dock, undock and arrival events, never per frame; each is charged to the arrival or dock budget and SP-YSORT-1 measures `R_flip` for the largest root (V9'). If `R_flip` is over budget the remedy is Alternative 10 together with retaining hidden scenes (OQ-F).

input.old_string:
draw calls follow texture runs along the sorted order (V8), and with one sheet per layer the sorted layer is a handful of runs per row in view; the GDD's own 50 to 300 estimate is "NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike". The decision rule is the GDD's, made explicit:

- **Trigger.** `D_ysort` (the world viewport's draw calls attributable to `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors`, measured by hiding those groups in a dev harness and reading `RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` per viewport) exceeds about 300 on a release export at the default field or at the largest ladder field.
input.new_string:
draw calls follow texture runs along the sorted order (V8), and the real driver of `D_ysort` is the **number of distinct textures per row across `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors`**: actors, items, horror rigs and trails use other sheets, so one atlas per layer does **not** bound it. "A handful of runs per row" is an expectation that needs measuring, not something V8 shows; the GDD's own 50 to 300 estimate is "NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike". SP-YSORT-1 therefore reports **distinct textures per row in the sorted band alongside `D_ysort`**. The decision rule is the GDD's, made explicit:

- **Trigger.** `D_ysort` (the world viewport's draw calls attributable to `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors`, measured in a dev harness and read as `RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` per viewport) exceeds about 300 on a release export at the default field or at the largest ladder field. **Measurement rules (E4, CT-56):** hiding or showing a group rebuilds its layers (V10 e), so a naive hide/show diff mixes rebuild frames with steady-state frames; the harness reads the count only **after the show has settled for at least 2 frames**, or diffs against a dev flag that skips adding the groups instead of toggling `visible`. Whether `get_render_info` is populated on a release export is **UNVERIFIED** and gated on SP-YSORT-1; ADR-0008 owns the draw-call table.

draw calls follow texture runs along the sorted order (V8), and the real driver of `D_ysort` is the **number of distinct textures per row across `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors`**: actors, items, horror rigs and trails use other sheets, so one atlas per layer does **not** bound it. "A handful of runs per row" is an expectation that needs measuring, not something V8 shows; the GDD's own 50 to 300 estimate is "NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike". SP-YSORT-1 therefore reports **distinct textures per row in the sorted band alongside `D_ysort`**. The decision rule is the GDD's, made explicit:

- **Trigger.** `D_ysort` (the world viewport's draw calls attributable to `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors`, measured in a dev harness and read as `RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` per viewport) exceeds about 300 on a release export at the default field or at the largest ladder field. **Measurement rules (E4, CT-56):** hiding or showing a group rebuilds its layers (V10 e), so a naive hide/show diff mixes rebuild frames with steady-state frames; the harness reads the count only **after the show has settled for at least 2 frames**, or diffs against a dev flag that skips adding the groups instead of toggling `visible`. Whether `get_render_info` is populated on a release export is **UNVERIFIED** and gated on SP-YSORT-1; ADR-0008 owns the draw-call table.

The orphan monitor is unverified on a release export; the release-safe check is the `ProjectorAudit.enumerate_into` tree walk.
- **R10: Float32 exactness of body offsets.** Offsets are bounded by ADR-0015's `BODY_COORD_LIMIT` (at most 2^24) and the canvas bound `|world_a - world_b| + |pos| < 2^23` under `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX` (otherwise `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` is lowered), CT-24; the release-export probe is ADR-0008's.

- **R12: A mobile owner forgets `rebind`.** The node is moved with the wrong component after a cut until the owner rebinds. content.thinking: I notice Alt 3's title still references "Alternative 5" oddly, but that's fine, and Alt 1's Cons and Alt 8 look untouched too. Now I'm moving on to editing the Consequences & Risks section.

input.old_string: - The weld and cut frames do work proportional to nodes moved, with no tile build and no gap; the bead appears in the first frame.
input.new_string: - The weld and cut frames do work proportional to nodes moved and cells re-rendered, with no tile re-authored and no gap; the bead appears in the first frame.

input.old_string: - A y-sorted `TileMapLayer` costs 0.39 ms to update 453 cells on the dev machine (V9), against 13 us unsorted; acceptable margin on a desktop, unproven on Deck.
input.new_string:
- A y-sorted `TileMapLayer` costs 0.39 ms to update 453 cells on the dev machine (V9), against 13 us unsorted; acceptable margin on a desktop, unproven on Deck.
- The engine rebuilds every cell of a `TileMapLayer` that is reparented or shown (V10): a weld or cut pays about 0.9 us per cell per moved layer, a mount pays a full unchunked build, and every WM-19 `BodyRoot.visible` flip to true pays a rebuild of the root's layers. `Staging` does not pre-warm rendering, so `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` bounds only the data work of an arrival.
- The guard surface (lints, `ProjectorAudit`, the specified-not-built fallback, the cross-body exception) is heavy for a small team; the tree-walk checks are merged into one boot/test walk (Validation Criteria) so only the lexical lints stay separate.

input.old_string:
- **R4: `D_ysort` exceeds the budget with real art (96 px faces break texture runs per row).** Mitigation: the § 10 rule; per-field draw caps in ADR-0008 § 7; the fallback is specified.
- **R5: The weld frame or an arrival exceeds budget on Deck.** Mitigation: the unit is data (`BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`), the weld does no tile work, and a hitch is bounded by `WELD_FRAME_HITCH_MAX_MS`; a second ladder rung is to move the shift of far sprites into the next frame, which the equal-key rule tolerates only within a body.
input.new_string:
- **R4: `D_ysort` exceeds the budget with real art (96 px faces break texture runs per row).** The driver is the number of distinct textures per row across `Faces`, `Mounted` and `PropsActors` (actors, items, horror rigs and trails use other sheets), which one atlas per layer does not bound. Mitigation: SP-YSORT-1 reports distinct textures per row alongside `D_ysort`; the § 10 rule; per-field draw caps in ADR-0008 § 7; the fallback is specified.
- **R5: The weld frame or an arrival exceeds budget on Deck.** The weld re-authors no tile, but the engine rebuilds the moved layers once, deferred (V10), unchunked, proportional to cells moved and unmeasured for Deck; a mount and a WM-19 show pay the same. Mitigation: the unit is data (`BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`), `R_weld`, `R_mount` and `R_flip` are measured by SP-YSORT-1 (V9'), a hitch is bounded by `WELD_FRAME_HITCH_MAX_MS`, `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` includes the mount frames, and the remedy is Alternative 10 (a permanent per-section parent) plus retained hidden scenes (OQ-F); a further rung is to move the position writes of far sprites into the next frame, which the equal-key rule tolerates only within a body.

input.old_string:
- **R9: Orphan noise.** A staged subtree outside the tree counts as orphans (V7). Mitigation: `Staging` is in the tree and hidden.
- **R10: Float32 exactness of body offsets.** Offsets are bounded by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (ADR-0015); the release-export probe is ADR-0008's.
input.new_string:
- **R9: Orphan noise, and the false comfort of staging.** A staged subtree outside the tree counts as orphans in the editor and debug runner (V7), so `Staging` is in the tree and hidden; but a layer built under a hidden parent builds nothing (V10 f), so staging pre-builds data only and the real build lands at mount. The orphan monitor is unverified on a release export; the release-safe check is the `ProjectorAudit.enumerate_into` tree walk.
- **R10: Float32 exactness of body offsets.** Offsets are bounded by ADR-0015's `BODY_COORD_LIMIT` (at most 2^24) and the canvas bound `|world_a - world_b| + |pos| < 2^23` under `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX` (otherwise `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` is lowered), CT-24; the release-export probe is ADR-0008's.
- **R11: A parked attachment is never re-mounted or told it is orphaned.** Mitigation: the parking step keeps the registration, `on_orphaned` is mandatory-callable at `attach`, `PJT_ATTACH_ORPHANED` counts unanswered parks, and the restore validation row checks every attachment's parent.
- **R12: A mobile owner forgets `rebind`.** The node is moved with the wrong component after a cut until the owner rebinds. Mitigation: obligation recorded on ADR-0023, ADR-0020 and ADR-0027; the `projector_stale_binding` dev counter; the owner's same-frame write makes the error invisible, not absent.

input.old_string: - **Order (auto, headless where pure):** `SortedLayer` property test: random inserts and merges give `(class_rank, entity_id)` order; the order is identical on 10 runs and after a rebuild that reverses creation order (PR-5 acceptance; AC-123 (b) within one body); a duplicate id is refused and counted.
input.new_string: - **Order (auto, headless where pure):** `SortedLayer` property test: random inserts and merges give `(class_rank, entity_id)` order with the `LayerOrder` prefix base; the order is identical on 10 runs and after a rebuild that reverses creation order (PR-5 acceptance; AC-123 (b) within one body); a duplicate id is refused and counted. **Order signature (T4):** incremental weld, cut and pod sequences versus a fresh `ALL` build, compared as an **ordered child list per group** (tile layers ascending by `section_id`, then sprites by `(class_rank, entity_id)`), including after a save and reload that reverses build order.

input.old_string:
- **Weld, cut, pod (integration with a scene harness, AC-BDY-92, AC-BDY-92b):** exactly one root per live body; after a weld the absorbed root is gone and node count equals the pre-weld count minus one with `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` flat; the Presenter's parent is the destination `PropsActors` in the same tick; draw order for an actor one pixel south and north of a wall edge before, on and after each transfer is unchanged.
- **Equivalence (auto):** a scripted weld, cut and pod sequence through an incremental projector and a fresh one fed `ALL` give equal `rebuild_signature()` (AC-121: the multiset of `(entity_id, kind_ordinal, position, size)` equals a live build).
- **No forbidden classes (auto, AC-122):** zero `CollisionShape2D`, `CollisionPolygon2D`, tile-set physics layer, `NavigationRegion2D`, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`; no `Camera2D` anywhere under `World`; no `Camera2D.limit_*` write.
input.new_string:
- **Weld, cut, pod (integration with a scene harness, AC-BDY-92, AC-BDY-92b):** exactly one root per live body; after a weld the absorbed root is gone and the **tree-walk node count** (`ProjectorAudit.enumerate_into`, the release-safe check) equals the pre-weld count minus one; in the editor or debug runner (gdUnit4) the `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` **delta** is zero (the monitor is never a release-export gate and its release availability is UNVERIFIED, V7); the Presenter's parent is the destination `PropsActors` in the same tick; draw order for an actor one pixel south and north of a wall edge before, on and after each transfer is unchanged. **Weld test (T1):** a socket sprite built in the same frame as the weld has the same position as in a fresh `ALL` build; no sprite is displaced twice.
- **Restore (integration, CT-33):** after a restore, every foreign attachment (Avatar Presenter, Trail, Interaction, Horror, Suit) is under the right body root (tree walk), `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` delta is zero in the editor or debug runner, the tree-walk node count equals a fresh build plus the attachments, no frame draws a partial interior (the load hold lasts until `ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()`), and an attachment whose section no longer exists received `on_orphaned`.
- **BODY_TRANSFER pass (integration, CT-32):** a pod hop and a weld re-base leave zero frames in which a beam `Light2D`'s parent is not `BodyRoot(body_of_actor(actor))` and zero reparented nodes without an owner position write before draw; `rebind` of a mobile non-actor attachment moves it to the new body in the same frame.
- **Sprite placement (T8):** toggling a door leaves the drawn rect (`position + offset`) unchanged while `sort_y` moves by `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`.
- **Equivalence (auto):** a scripted weld, cut and pod sequence through an incremental projector and a fresh one fed `ALL` give equal `rebuild_signature()` (AC-121: the multiset of `(entity_id, kind_ordinal, position, size)` equals a live build, **and** the ordered child list per group is equal).
- **No forbidden classes (auto, AC-122):** zero `CollisionShape2D`, `CollisionPolygon2D`, tile-set physics layer, `NavigationRegion2D`, `LightOccluder2D`, and no `Light2D` created or parented by the projectors except nodes attached through `attach_light`; no `Camera2D` anywhere under `World`; no `Camera2D.limit_*` write.

input.old_string: - **Limits (auto):** the rectangle equals the union formula for one, two and three sections,
input.new_string: - **Limits (auto):** the rectangle equals the bounding-box formula for one, two and three sections,

input.old_string: - **Build rate (auto + perf):** the arrival scene builds in exactly `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)` frames with `U` counted from real `build_section` output;
input.new_string: - **Build rate (auto + perf):** the arrival scene builds its data in exactly `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)` frames with `U` counted from real `build_section` output, then mounts one scene per `present` (`+ S` frames);

input.old_string:
- **Performance (perf, release export, RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK):** weld frame P99 at most the 8 ms working threshold over 100 welds; steady-state stage-0 proposal; `D_ysort` reported per viewport with the fallback trigger of § 10.
- **Lint pack `PJT-01` to `PJT-10` (ADR-0010 owns the tool and the tier; proposed here):** `PJT-01` body roots and `World` are `y_sort_enabled`, translation only (tree walk); `PJT-02` the group set and order under a body root; `PJT-03` `z_index` written only in the group builder, no z literal; `PJT-04` no one-argument `.reparent(`, parent changes only through `SceneMove`; `PJT-05` no `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`, collision or navigation class in `src/presentation/projector/`; `PJT-06` no `queue_free`/`free` of an attached node by its owner without `detach`; `PJT-07` `Camera2D` absent under `World`, no `limit_` write; `PJT-08` `EntityId.pack` takes a name from `EntityNs`, never a literal; `PJT-09` no `load(` / `preload(` inside a `present` callable; `PJT-10` every `TileSet` built by `TileSetCache` has one atlas source.
input.new_string:
- **Performance (perf, release export, RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK):** weld frame P99 at most the 8 ms working threshold over 100 welds, measured as `R_weld` (reparent plus the following frame or `update_internals()`, real cell counts, windowed), with `R_mount` and `R_flip` reported; steady-state stage-0 proposal; `D_ysort` and distinct textures per row reported per viewport with the fallback trigger of § 10, read after a 2-frame settle; `get_render_info` and the orphan monitor availability on a release export reported as found (UNVERIFIED until then).
- **Audit and lint pack (ADR-0010 owns the tool and the tier; proposed here, T11):** the structural checks that a tree can answer are **one `ProjectorAudit` boot or test tree walk**, formerly `PJT-01`, `-02`, `-05`, `-07` and `-10`: body roots and `World` are `y_sort_enabled` and translation only; the group set and order under a body root, and in each group the tile layers precede the sprites and are ascending by `section_id`; no `LightOccluder2D`, collision or navigation node, and no `Light2D` outside `attach_light`; `Camera2D` absent under `World`; every `TileSet` built by `TileSetCache` has one atlas source. The **lexical lints** that a tree walk cannot see stay: `PJT-03` `z_index` written only in the group builder, no z literal; `PJT-04` no one-argument `.reparent(`, parent changes only through `SceneMove`; `PJT-06` no `queue_free`/`free` of an attached node by its owner without `detach`; `PJT-08` `EntityId.pack` takes a name from `EntityNs`, never a literal; `PJT-09` no `load(` / `preload(` inside a `present` callable.

cat > /tmp/adr34_tail.txt <<'EOF'
## Registry Candidates
- state_ownership `projector_scene_tree`: owner Layout projector and `body.projector` (`src/presentation/projector/`); the `ProjectorRoot`, `Staging`, `World`, `BodyRoot`s, band groups, `SectionScene`s, `TileSet`s. Interface: the `BodyScenes` mutation facade (`attach`, `attach_presenter`, `attach_light`, `detach`, `rebind`; no getter) and `SectionScene` handles; the Layout projector creates nodes only in `Staging` or through `SectionScene` methods and all parenting and `SortedLayer` insertion under a body root is `body.projector`'s. Never persisted, never hashed.
- interfaces `projector_attach_api`: `BodyScenes.attach(body_id, band, node, class_rank, entity_id, section_id, on_orphaned) -> int`, `detach(node)`, `attach_presenter(actor_id, node)`, `attach_light(actor_id, beam_id, node)` (parent is the `BodyRoot`), `rebind(node, body_id, section_id) -> int`; foreign nodes are parked in `Staging` before any root is freed and `on_orphaned` is called when their body or section is gone.
- interfaces `camera_limits_sink`: `CameraLimits {valid, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y, body_id, epoch}`, the raw hull bounding box, written only by `body.projector` in stage `PROJECT`; `rect_eff`, the clamp order, `CLAMPED` and JOLT are ADR-0008's (asked to take them explicitly).
- interfaces `projector_readiness`: `ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()` read by `PipelineRoot` for the TRANSIT_HOLD latch and for the load hold (held until ready).
- interfaces `entity_id_namespaces`: `EntityId.pack(ns, local)`; namespace bytes LAYOUT 1, BODY 2, INTERACTION 3, HORROR 4, SUIT 5, WEB 6, TRAIL 7, LIGHTING 8 (a registration key, not a sort key); append-only with a golden test, never renumbered; `kind_ordinal` DOOR_LEAF 1, PROP 2, MACHINE 3, BEAD 4, PLATE 5, SCAR 6, JAMB 7.
- api_decisions `y_sort_scope_merged`: nested `y_sort_enabled` ancestors form one scope; ties by tree order; tile cell key formula; sort origin set per layer; a group's tile layers are a prefix in ascending `section_id` (LayerOrder) before its sorted sprites; same-row cells of one layer tie by x.
- api_decisions `z_band_names`: `ZBand` FLOOR 0, MARKS 1, YSORT 10, CAPS 20, DUST 30; dependents use names; lights' `range_z` must cover FLOOR to DUST.
- api_decisions `scene_move_primitive`: `SceneMove.to` (`reparent(p, false)`) is the only parent-change primitive; on 4.7.2 reparenting or showing a `TileMapLayer` makes the engine rebuild every cell once, deferred, and that cost is the weld budget term.
- forbidden_patterns `one_arg_node_reparent`, `merged_per_body_tilemaplayer`, `sort_tiebreak_by_x_or_creation_order`, `projector_builds_into_body_root_directly`, `free_root_with_foreign_attachments`.
- performance_budgets `projector_weld_frame`: 8 ms P99 working threshold including the engine rebuild of moved layers (`R_weld`), release export, UNVERIFIED; arrival build `ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME) + S` frames.
- referenced_by_update: `camera_canvas_transform_write`, `presentation_stage_and_placement`, `source_layout_layer_first_tree`.

## GDD Sync
- `pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` PR-5 sort origin: "the wall-face `TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin` `[BIN]` is set to the footprint depth, not 0" becomes "the engine key of a tile is `cell_top + tile_h/2 + y_sort_origin` (probed 2026-10-29); wall-face and wall-mounted layers use cell height `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` and a layer `y_sort_origin` of `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH / 2`, so the key is the footprint's south edge".
- `pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` Y-sort lint AC: "the wall-face `TileMapLayer` has `y_sort_origin == 24`" and "the cap `TileMapLayer` is not a child of the Y-sort node" become "the effective sort key of a wall-face tile equals its footprint south edge" and "no node in the Floor, Marks, Caps or Dust band has `y_sort_enabled` or is a descendant of a sorted group".
- `pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` PR-5 "ONE `Node2D`": reworded to "one merged Y-sort scope: nested `y_sort_enabled` nodes sort as one group (probed); each body root is `y_sort_enabled`; band values are `ZBand` names; camera limits (C8) add the north overhang".
- `ship-body-and-interior-physics.md` BDY-33 (d) and AC-BDY-92b: the body root is itself `y_sort_enabled`; it owns seven band groups, of which the actor/props layer is `PropsActors`, preceded by `Faces` and `Mounted`; (f) the move uses `SceneMove.to` (`reparent(parent, false)`), which keeps the local position, the owning presenter rewrites the position in the same frame, `BodyScenes.rebind` serves mobile non-actor nodes and beam lights attach through `attach_light`; "Layout's section nodes ... siblings" becomes "the Layout projector builds section scenes in `Staging` and `body.projector` mounts them".
- `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-31 and the engine feasibility note: the default shape is decided (per-body roots, per-section layers, reparent and recompute positions); "tests option B first" is replaced by "SP-YSORT-1 confirms the decided shape"; `LAYOUT_ID_NS = 1`, packing in `src/shared/entity_id.gd`; `JAMB` is `kind_ordinal` 7 (added to ADR-0013 § 13's closed vocabulary); OQ-33 closed.
- `web-map-and-transit.md` WM-19: the draw rule is realised as `BodyRoot.visible` driven by a Web Map read of the docked set; each false-to-true flip rebuilds the root's layers (`R_flip`); D.13 numerator: `ceil(tiles_max / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME)` becomes the projector's work-unit count `U` (tiles plus sprites, § 6) of the largest destination scene plus one mount frame per scene `S`, computed by a test from real `build_section` output.
- `design/registry/entities.yaml`: `LAYOUT_ID_NS` value 1 (was "to be agreed with the Pipeline owner"); add the `EntityNs` table (BODY 2, INTERACTION 3, HORROR 4, SUIT 5, WEB 6, TRAIL 7, LIGHTING 8; append-only); `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` formula numerator is `U` plus the mount frames `S`.
- `derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` DA-5: "the PROJECTOR picks an atlas by `template_id`" names its source, `assets/data/presentation/atlas_map.json` (`template_id` to MAINTAINED or WORN), boot lints `ATLAS_MAP_TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN` and `ATLAS_MAP_MISSING`; no Layout field carries wear.

## Review Log

**2026-10-29. Per-ADR engine and TD-ADR reviews (CONCERNS, 1 blocking) and Core-tier cross-ADR adjudication. Status stays Proposed. One line per finding or ruling.**
- **E1 (high, BLOCKING): applied.** Reworded the Summary, Requirements, § 1 table, § 7 Decision, Alternative 4, Consequences, R5, § 11 and Performance to "no tile is re-authored; the engine rebuilds the moved layers' canvas items once, deferred". Added V10 (the review probe a to g) and corrected V9 as call-only. Replaced the reparent figure with `R_weld` (reparent plus the following frame or `update_internals()`, real cell counts, windowed, release export, RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK) as the weld budget term (V9', § 11). Mount rebuild declared unchunked, one scene per `present`, counted as `+ S` frames in the arrival formula (§ 6, not in units). Stated that `Staging` is a data stage only (§ 6, Summary, R9). Added Alternative 10 (permanent per-section parent, zero-rebuild), rejected for now with a revisit trigger (OQ-I). Stated WM-19 uses `BodyRoot.visible`, that each false-to-true flip rebuilds the root's layers, and that SP-YSORT-1 measures `R_flip` (§ 8).
- **E2 (medium): applied.** Added the LayerOrder step and `LayerOrder` class (tile layers a prefix of each group in ascending `section_id`), `SortedLayer` index base `layers.count()` (§ 3.3, § 7 step 2 and 3), and the `ProjectorAudit` tree-walk check and ordered-child `rebuild_signature` for "layers precede sprites, layers by section_id".
- **E3 (medium): applied.** V7, § 7, R9 and Validation: orphan assertions are deltas in the editor or debug runner (gdUnit4); the monitor is never a release gate and its release availability is marked UNVERIFIED; `ProjectorAudit.enumerate_into` is the release-safe node count.
- **E4 (low): applied.** `get_render_info` release availability marked UNVERIFIED and gated on SP-YSORT-1 (ADR-0008 owns the table) in V8, § 10, § 11; the harness reads after a 2-frame settle or diffs against a dev flag that skips adding the groups.
- **E5 (low): applied.** One signature, `DoorSort.sort_y(y0, open_extent_px)`, in § 3.1, Key Interfaces and the TR-pxl-007 row.

decisions.chosen: Keep reparent-and-recompute-positions as the decision; record the per-section permanent parent as Alternative 10, rejected for now with a revisit trigger on measured R_weld
decisions.reason: Per-section parents only remove the weld half of the engine rebuild (a WM-19 visible flip still rebuilds), break the registered per-body root shape (BDY-33, AC-BDY-92), and R_weld is about 0.4 ms for 453 sorted cells on the dev machine against an 8 ms threshold; the BodyScenes facade keeps the switch local.

decisions.point: Mount rebuild: chunk or declare unchunked (E1)
decisions.chosen: Declared unchunked, one scene mounted per present call, counted as +S frames in the arrival formula (U stays data units); Staging stated as a data stage only
decisions.reason: The engine builds nothing for a layer not visible in the tree and builds all cells in one deferred burst when it first becomes visible, so BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME cannot bound it; ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS is sized to ceil(U/B)+S and the burst time is measured by SP-YSORT-1.

decisions.chosen: BodyRoot.visible kept; every false-to-true flip rebuilds the root's layers (R_flip) and is measured; remedy is Alternative 10 plus retained hidden scenes
decisions.reason: Hiding costs nothing, flips happen only on dock, undock and arrival events, and freeing and rebuilding on each flip would cost strictly more.

decisions.chosen: Park every foreign attachment in Staging with its registration before any free, re-mount on return, on_orphaned for the vanished; restore rebuilt under the ADR-0008 load hold held until ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()
decisions.reason: Covers cold loads from the title screen where no old roots exist, costs one condition in ADR-0008, and the option of keeping old roots drawing was rejected by the adjudication.

decisions.point: Position ownership of foreign nodes after a move (CT-32, T7)
decisions.chosen: Actor-following nodes, LIGHTING nodes and Horror rigs are position-written by their owners in the same frame; section-bound static attachments (Trail marks, items) are re-placed by the projector as a flagged exception (OQ-H)
decisions.reason: Those owners write only on their own dirty keys, so without the shift a static mark would be displaced after a weld; the exception is stated and ADR-0009 is asked to sanction it or the owners to take it over.

decisions.chosen: Store section-local rects once at build; position = section_offset + local_origin through Placement.put, recomputed from the current offset, never position + delta
decisions.reason: section_rects_into rows are already body-frame occupied spans, so delta arithmetic double-shifts sprites built after a weld and breaks staged builds that straddle a re-base.

decisions.chosen: LayerOrder step: tile layers are a prefix of each group in ascending section_id, SortedLayer index base = layers.count(), ordered child list in rebuild_signature
decisions.reason: reparent appends as last child, so weld history would otherwise decide ties and change after save and reload.

decisions.chosen: attach_light with EntityNs.LIGHTING 8 as a registration key, parent is the BodyRoot, reparented with the Presenter in one stage-0 pass before stage AVATAR
decisions.reason: Ruling CT-32; the beam light's frame was unowned and reparent(p, false) plus an owner rewrite in the same frame keeps the projector from writing the position.

decisions.chosen: Applied: PJT-01/02/05/07/10 merged into one ProjectorAudit tree walk; PJT-03/04/06/08/09 kept as lexical lints
decisions.reason: A tree walk already enumerates what those five check, so separate lints are duplicate machinery for a small team; lexical checks a walk cannot see are kept.

decisions.chosen: Dropped the five-publisher agreement; namespace table append-only with golden test; acceptance gated on SP-YSORT-1 and ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 Accepted
decisions.reason: The publisher ADRs are later tiers that list this ADR as an input, so the condition was circular.

decisions.chosen: Keep reparent-and-recompute-positions as the decision; record the per-section permanent parent as Alternative 10, rejected for now with a revisit trigger on measured R_weld
decisions.reason: Per-section parents only remove the weld half of the engine rebuild (a WM-19 visible flip still rebuilds), break the registered per-body root shape (BDY-33, AC-BDY-92), and R_weld is about 0.4 ms for 453 sorted cells on the dev machine against an 8 ms threshold; the BodyScenes facade keeps the switch local.

decisions.point: Mount rebuild: chunk or declare unchunked (E1)
decisions.chosen: Declared unchunked, one scene mounted per present call, counted as +S frames in the arrival formula (U stays data units); Staging stated as a data stage only
decisions.reason: The engine builds nothing for a layer not visible in the tree and builds all cells in one deferred burst when it first becomes visible, so BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME cannot bound it; ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS is sized to ceil(U/B)+S and the burst time is measured by SP-YSORT-1.

decisions.chosen: BodyRoot.visible kept; every false-to-true flip rebuilds the root's layers (R_flip) and is measured; remedy is Alternative 10 plus retained hidden scenes
decisions.reason: Hiding costs nothing, flips happen only on dock, undock and arrival events, and freeing and rebuilding on each flip would cost strictly more.

decisions.chosen: Park every foreign attachment in Staging with its registration before any free, re-mount on return, on_orphaned for the vanished; restore rebuilt under the ADR-0008 load hold held until ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()
decisions.reason: Covers cold loads from the title screen where no old roots exist, costs one condition in ADR-0008, and the option of keeping old roots drawing was rejected by the adjudication.

decisions.point: Position ownership of foreign nodes after a move (CT-32, T7)
decisions.chosen: Actor-following nodes, LIGHTING nodes and Horror rigs are position-written by their owners in the same frame; section-bound static attachments (Trail marks, items) are re-placed by the projector as a flagged exception (OQ-H)
decisions.reason: Those owners write only on their own dirty keys, so without the shift a static mark would be displaced after a weld; the exception is stated and ADR-0009 is asked to sanction it or the owners to take it over.

decisions.chosen: Store section-local rects once at build; position = section_offset + local_origin through Placement.put, recomputed from the current offset, never position + delta
decisions.reason: section_rects_into rows are already body-frame occupied spans, so delta arithmetic double-shifts sprites built after a weld and breaks staged builds that straddle a re-base.

decisions.chosen: LayerOrder step: tile layers are a prefix of each group in ascending section_id, SortedLayer index base = layers.count(), ordered child list in rebuild_signature
decisions.reason: reparent appends as last child, so weld history would otherwise decide ties and change after save and reload.

decisions.chosen: attach_light with EntityNs.LIGHTING 8 as a registration key, parent is the BodyRoot, reparented with the Presenter in one stage-0 pass before stage AVATAR
decisions.reason: Ruling CT-32; the beam light's frame was unowned and reparent(p, false) plus an owner rewrite in the same frame keeps the projector from writing the position.

decisions.chosen: Applied: PJT-01/02/05/07/10 merged into one ProjectorAudit tree walk; PJT-03/04/06/08/09 kept as lexical lints
decisions.reason: A tree walk already enumerates what those five check, so separate lints are duplicate machinery for a small team; lexical checks a walk cannot see are kept.

decisions.chosen: Dropped the five-publisher agreement; namespace table append-only with golden test; acceptance gated on SP-YSORT-1 and ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 Accepted
decisions.reason: The publisher ADRs are later tiers that list this ADR as an input, so the condition was circular.

- purpose: scene_move_primitive
    status: active           # ADR-0034 is Proposed; ADR-0009 is asked to reword its reparent sanction
    api: "SceneMove.to(node, new_parent) = node.reparent(new_parent, false) is the only way presentation changes a node's parent; the local position is kept (probed), the node becomes the last child, LayerOrder and SortedLayer restore order; positions are recomputed through Placement.put; on 4.7.2 reparenting or showing a TileMapLayer makes the engine rebuild every cell once, deferred (about 0.9 us per cell on the dev machine), and that rebuild is the weld budget term R_weld"
    not: "Node.reparent(parent) with the default keep_global_transform = true (rewrites the local position); freeing a node another presenter attached; treating the reparent call time as the weld cost; position + delta arithmetic for sprites"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0034-projector-scene-shape-and-y-sort.md
    reason: "TR-shipbody-032 forbids global-transform-preserving reparent; Placement.put is the one integer assignment point; probe V10 shows the rebuild lands in the deferred update"

gdd_sync.old: PR-5 Sort origin: the wall-face `TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin` `[BIN]` is set to the footprint depth, not 0
gdd_sync.new: The engine key of a tile is cell_top + tile_h/2 + y_sort_origin (probed 2026-10-29); wall-face and wall-mounted layers use cell height WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH and a layer y_sort_origin of WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH/2, so the key is the footprint's south edge

gdd_sync.old: Y-sort lint AC: the wall-face TileMapLayer has y_sort_origin == 24; the cap TileMapLayer is not a child of the Y-sort node
gdd_sync.new: The effective sort key of a wall-face tile equals its footprint south edge; no node in the Floor, Marks, Caps or Dust band has y_sort_enabled or is a descendant of a sorted group (by band, not ancestry)

decisions.chosen: Keep reparent-and-recompute-positions as the decision; record the per-section permanent parent as Alternative 10, rejected for now with a revisit trigger on measured R_weld
decisions.reason: Per-section parents only remove the weld half of the engine rebuild (a WM-19 visible flip still rebuilds), break the registered per-body root shape (BDY-33, AC-BDY-92), and R_weld is about 0.4 ms for 453 sorted cells on the dev machine against an 8 ms threshold; the BodyScenes facade keeps the switch local.

decisions.point: Mount rebuild: chunk or declare unchunked (E1)
decisions.chosen: Declared unchunked, one scene mounted per present call, counted as +S frames in the arrival formula (U stays data units); Staging stated as a data stage only
decisions.reason: The engine builds nothing for a layer not visible in the tree and builds all cells in one deferred burst when it first becomes visible, so BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME cannot bound it; ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS is sized to ceil(U/B)+S and the burst time is measured by SP-YSORT-1.

decisions.chosen: BodyRoot.visible kept; every false-to-true flip rebuilds the root's layers (R_flip) and is measured; remedy is Alternative 10 plus retained hidden scenes
decisions.reason: Hiding costs nothing, flips happen only on dock, undock and arrival events, and freeing and rebuilding on each flip would cost strictly more.

decisions.chosen: Park every foreign attachment in Staging with its registration before any free, re-mount on return, on_orphaned for the vanished; restore rebuilt under the ADR-0008 load hold held until ProjectorReadiness.is_ready()
decisions.reason: Covers cold loads from the title screen where no old roots exist, costs one condition in ADR-0008, and the option of keeping old roots drawing was rejected by the adjudication.

decisions.point: Position ownership of foreign nodes after a move (CT-32, T7)
decisions.chosen: Actor-following nodes, LIGHTING nodes and Horror rigs are position-written by their owners in the same frame; section-bound static attachments (Trail marks, items) are re-placed by the projector as a flagged exception (OQ-H)
decisions.reason: Those owners write only on their own dirty keys, so without the shift a static mark would be displaced after a weld; the exception is stated and ADR-0009 is asked to sanction it or the owners to take it over.

decisions.chosen: Store section-local rects once at build; position = section_offset + local_origin through Placement.put, recomputed from the current offset, never position + delta
decisions.reason: section_rects_into rows are already body-frame occupied spans, so delta arithmetic double-shifts sprites built after a weld and breaks staged builds that straddle a re-base.

decisions.chosen: LayerOrder step: tile layers are a prefix of each group in ascending section_id, SortedLayer index base = layers.count(), ordered child list in rebuild_signature
decisions.reason: reparent appends as last child, so weld history would otherwise decide ties and change after save and reload.

decisions.chosen: attach_light with EntityNs.LIGHTING 8 as a registration key, parent is the BodyRoot, reparented with the Presenter in one stage-0 pass before stage AVATAR
decisions.reason: Ruling CT-32; the beam light's frame was unowned and reparent(p, false) plus an owner rewrite in the same frame keeps the projector from writing the position.

decisions.chosen: Applied: PJT-01/02/05/07/10 merged into one ProjectorAudit tree walk; PJT-03/04/06/08/09 kept as lexical lints
decisions.reason: A tree walk already enumerates what those five check, so separate lints are duplicate machinery for a small team; lexical checks a walk cannot see are kept.

decisions.chosen: Dropped the five-publisher agreement; namespace table append-only with golden test; acceptance gated on SP-YSORT-1 and ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 Accepted
decisions.reason: The publisher ADRs are later tiers that list this ADR as an input, so the condition was circular.

open_questions: OQ-A: ProjectionSet source (ADR-0026 projection_sections_into) is still an assumption.
OQ-B: Docked input for WM-19 InteriorDrawRule is assumed to be a Web Map read.
OQ-D: Wall tile cell width and x pitch for 24 px footprints is an art and asset-spec decision.
OQ-F: Retaining departed hidden scenes is not built; revisit if arrival or R_flip is over budget.
OQ-G: Cross-body equal-key ties follow body order; adopt Alternative 2 if SP-YSORT-1 shows a visible flip.
OQ-H: ADR-0009 write list must allow the projector to re-place section-bound static foreign attachments on weld and cut, or their owners take that over and the exception is deleted.
OQ-I: If SP-YSORT-1 measures R_weld or R_flip over budget, adopt Alternative 10 with retained hidden scenes and change BDY-33 and AC-BDY-92 wording.

OQ-J: /architecture-review sync items: traceability index lists 2 rows for ADR-0034 versus 14 plus owned-elsewhere rows, and the TR-pxl-017 row attributes rect_eff and clamp rules to ADR-0034 instead of ADR-0008.
Closed: OQ-C (JAMB 7) and OQ-E (area_max invariant) by CT-14.
UNVERIFIED and gated on SP-YSORT-1: release-export availability of OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT and Viewport.get_render_info; R_weld, R_mount and R_flip on release exports and RM-DECK.
